## Summary

Add a new "Step 0: Work-item audit gate" to the cleanup skill instructions (`skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`) that invokes the audit skill when the current branch has an associated work-item ID, before any branch operations begin.

## Context

The cleanup skill currently has no awareness of work-item lifecycle. This step gates the cleanup process on a work-item audit: if the branch has an associated work item, the audit skill is invoked first. The existing audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces structured verdicts (`met`/`unmet`/`partial`) that the agent uses to decide whether to proceed or abort.

This is a SKILL.md-only change — agent behavior instructions, no Python code changes.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (insert new Step 0 before current Step 1)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new "Step 0" is added before the existing Step 1 in `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
2. Step 0 instructs the agent to: check the `work_item_id` field from the `inspect_current_branch.py` JSON output, invoke the audit skill if an ID is found, and proceed or abort based on audit results
3. The step documents the decision rules: all criteria `met` -> proceed; any `unmet`/`partial` -> abort; no acceptance criteria defined -> abort
4. Existing steps 1-9 remain unchanged in behavior and order
5. Step 0 is skipped when no work-item ID is found (e.g., on `main` or branches without tokens)

## Minimal Implementation

- Insert a new section in SKILL.md before the current "1. Inspect current branch"
- Reference the audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) invocation pattern
- Document the decision rule: only proceed if every criterion has verdict `met`
- Document the skip logic when no work-item ID is present in the `inspect_current_branch.py` output

## Note

This task covers the audit gate structure. The status transition (on pass) and abort messaging (on failure) are covered by sibling tasks but may be implemented together since they all modify the same Step 0 section.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
data.title: Add audit gate step to cleanup skill

## Summary

Document in the cleanup skill instructions that when the audit passes (all criteria `met`), the agent should transition the work item to `status=completed, stage=in_review` and add a comment before proceeding with branch cleanup.

## Context

This follows the same transition pattern established by SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1 (implement-flow: mark work-item completed/in_review after merge). Consistency with that pattern ensures downstream processes (triage audit, producer review) work correctly.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0, after audit pass condition)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. SKILL.md Step 0 includes explicit `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` command to run after audit passes
2. The transition uses the same pattern as the implement-flow (SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1): status=completed, stage=in_review
3. A comment is added to the work item documenting that cleanup audit passed, including branch name context: `wl comment add <id> --comment "Cleanup audit passed on branch <branch-name>. Work item transitioned to in_review." --author <agent-name>`
4. The transition happens after the audit passes but before any branch operations begin (i.e., before Step 1)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add transition instructions to Step 0 in SKILL.md after the audit-pass decision point
- Include the exact `wl update` and `wl comment add` commands the agent should run
- Specify that this must happen before proceeding to Step 1

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and abort-behavior tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0)
data.title: Add status transition on audit pass

data.description:
## Summary

Define clear abort messaging in the cleanup skill for when the audit gate fails (criteria `unmet`/`partial`) or when no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item.

## Context

When the audit gate determines that cleanup should not proceed, the agent needs clear instructions on what to output and how to halt. There are two abort scenarios:
1. **Criteria unmet/partial:** The audit skill returns one or more criteria with `unmet` or `partial` verdicts.
2. **No acceptance criteria:** The work item has no acceptance criteria section defined, so the audit cannot verify completion.

Both scenarios result in a hard abort — no branch operations are performed.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When any criterion is `unmet` or `partial`, the agent outputs a clear message listing which criteria failed and their verdicts (referencing the audit report)
2. When no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item, the agent outputs a message explaining that the work item cannot be verified and cleanup is aborted
3. After abort, no branch operations are performed (steps 1-9 are all skipped entirely)
4. The abort message suggests next steps (e.g., "Fix the unmet criteria and re-run cleanup" or "Add acceptance criteria to the work item and re-run cleanup")

## Minimal Implementation

- Add abort message templates/examples to Step 0 in SKILL.md
- Document the "no acceptance criteria" abort case as a separate condition
- Document explicitly that the agent must not proceed to any subsequent step after abort
- Include example abort output for both scenarios

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and status-transition tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

Summary: Implement 'wl ampa config' subcommand providing show (default), set <key> <value>, and reset <key> with validation of keys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'wl ampa config' prints each config field, its effective value, and the source (env / persisted / default).
- 'wl ampa config set <key> <value>' persists overrides to scheduler_store.json and validates keys; unknown keys are rejected with a clear error.
- 'wl ampa config reset <key>' removes persisted overrides for that key.
- CLI operations respect local-operator-only constraints (file permissions / user ownership).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add subcommand in ampa/scheduler_cli.py following existing CLI pattern.
- Implement validation using SchedulerConfig fields.
- Persist via helper from Feature 1 and trigger SIGHUP on set/reset.
- Add unit tests for CLI parsing and persistence behavior.

## Deliverables
CLI code, tests, help text, docs update.

Summary: Extend command entries with allowed_hours and allowed_days, store windows in UTC, accept/validate ranges (including cross-midnight), and skip commands outside windows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Command schema includes allowed_hours (e.g., ['9-10','22-2']) and allowed_days (e.g., ['mon-fri']).
- Scheduler selection logic silently skips commands that are currently outside their window.
- Windows are accepted in local timezone on input, stored in UTC, and displayed in local timezone.
- Tests cover cross-midnight windows and DST boundary cases.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add fields to CommandSpec and SchedulerStore handling in ampa/scheduler.py.
- Implement parser for hour and day ranges and integrate checks into selection loop.
- Add unit tests for parsing and evaluation; integration test for skipping commands outside window.

## Deliverables
code changes, tests, schema doc update (ampa/scheduler_schema.md).

Summary: Add a SIGHUP handler in the scheduler daemon that reloads scheduler_store.json immediately so wl ampa config set takes effect without waiting for the next poll.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon installs a SIGHUP handler which reloads the store and new config atomically.
- CLI set/reset signals the running daemon (using existing PID file if present; otherwise a well-known pidfile).
- Reload does not interrupt in-progress runs (only changes selection criteria).
- Tests simulate SIGHUP and validate reload behavior.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add SIGHUP handler in ampa/daemon.py (or scheduler entrypoint) to call the store reload path.
- Update wl ampa config CLI to locate the scheduler PID (existing pidfile or well-known runtime pidfile).
- Add tests to assert in-memory config updates after SIGHUP.

## Deliverables
daemon signal handler, CLI signal code, tests, docs for operator flow.

## Audit Test Suite Refactoring

**Summary:** Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target the new descriptor-driven handler API. Add new test files for `AuditResult` dataclass/parser and handler unit tests. Maintain coverage for cooldown (caller concern), blocked items, Discord integration, and auto-completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Existing 13 test scenarios from `tests/test_triage_audit.py` are preserved or intentionally replaced with equivalent coverage targeting the new handler API
- [ ] New tests for `AuditResult` parsing (>=5 samples: pass, fail, malformed, empty, multi-AC)
- [ ] New tests for each handler covering: from-state validation, invariant evaluation, state transitions, error cases
- [ ] New tests for extended auto-completion checks (PR merge, CI status, PR comments, children, deps)
- [ ] All external calls mocked (`wl`, `opencode run`, `gh pr view`, `gh api`)
- [ ] Test coverage for audit-related code paths >= prior level as measured by `pytest --cov`
- [ ] Tests verify behavioral parity with descriptor definitions (not hardcoded heuristics)

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target new handler functions/classes
- New `tests/test_audit_result.py` for AuditResult dataclass and parser
- New `tests/test_audit_handlers.py` for handler-specific unit tests (if not covered by refactored file)
- Update mocking patterns to match new API (protocols, adapters)

## Dependencies

- SA-0MM8W4FQR0UY1NHQ (AuditResult dataclass)
- SA-0MM8W553C1WK7JE5 (audit_result handler)
- SA-0MM8W5EXT1BXC7PB (audit_fail handler)
- SA-0MM8W5U8C0QGGXTD (close_with_audit handler)
- SA-0MM8W69L91DJQY50 (routing — partial block for integration tests only)

## Deliverables

- Refactored test files
- New test files as needed
- Coverage report verification

## Reference Files

- `tests/test_triage_audit.py` — existing tests (1178 lines, 13 tests)
- `docs/workflow/test-plan.md` — TC-DL test specifications for audit scenarios
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` — audit failure flow reference

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (verified).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` contain: a `session` header event (start timestamp, cwd, id) and per-message assistant events with a `usage` object (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `totalTokens`, `cost`). Last event timestamp ≈ session end. Verified during intake.
- Baseline sample (SorraAgents sessions only, 2026-08-09): 69 sessions, ~30.5h total, avg 26.6 min/session, avg 3.8M total tokens/session (dominated by cache reads; total-token values include cache). One extreme outlier session (153 min, 146.9M total tokens) associated with repeated output-token-limit errors — the report must handle such outliers (report both mean and median).
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` exists but currently contains **no source files** (only `__pycache__`). If this is the "existing usage skill in the proxy" intended for measurement, it must be verified to actually run; otherwise the analysis script in this work item is authoritative.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` measures startup-context bytes — related (our change grows startup context by ~50 bytes) but does not measure session token usage. Run before/after to confirm the addition stays within `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` if that gate is enforced.

## Desired change

1. Add the sentence to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the worktree; commit to `dev`; record exact commit hash and wall-clock T0.
2. Let the experiment run 24h (T0 → T0+24h). No special agent behavior needed during the window beyond normal work.
3. At T0+24h: collect metrics for [T0−24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) across all projects; produce the comparison report; revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (new commit to `dev`); record revert hash.
4. Deliver: report (metrics table, deltas, outliers, interpretation), AC verification, session-log of the experiment itself.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — add then revert the STE sentence (the treatment).
- `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` — comparison report (new).
- `skill/ste100-experiment/scripts/analyze_sessions.py` (new, or revived `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/`) — deterministic analysis over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`; produces per-session duration/tokens and window aggregates + tests.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — verify/revive if the proxy-side usage skill is to be used for measurement.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` / `SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR` — "Reduce initial LLM context…" (completed + in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), context-budget angle. Our +1 sentence slightly increases startup context; keep within budget.
- `SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP` (F1) — "Startup-context measurement tooling": produced `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`; related measurement tooling, different axis.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size": also touches startup-context surface.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — intended measurement tool per operator; source currently missing, verify.
- `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO` — "Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md" (in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); session-traceability comments are how experiment sessions get identified/attributed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Null result risk:** a bare STE100 sentence may not change model output measurably (no vocabulary enforcement; model may not deeply know STE rules). A null result is a valid outcome — report it as such rather than extending the experiment.
- **Confounds:** session mix (project, work type, human vs automated, model, token-limit error loops) differs between windows; day-of-week/time-of-day effects. Mitigations: report medians alongside means, break down by project/model, describe composition, keep interpretation descriptive (correlation, not causation).
- **Boundary sessions:** sessions spanning T0 or T0+24h attributed by *start timestamp* (documented rule).
- **Measurement tooling uncertainty:** if the proxy usage skill is non-functional, the repo analysis script (AC 5) is authoritative — do not block on proxy tooling.
- **Left-over instruction:** the sentence must be reverted; AC 1 greps verify both states. Add a calendar/reminder if available to avoid the window overrunning.
- **Scope creep:** STE compliance scoring, dictionary enforcement, or policy changes are separate work items (`discovered-from:SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD` if created).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLGALPU80E5HBIJ** – Persist pending prompts to tool-output (completed)
- **SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO** – Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md (in-progress)
- **SA-0MM03YIY609CP27Y** – Scheduler Test Button Command (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-ste100-experiment-SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD.md` — matched: 24h, agent, agents, always, asd (+21 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which AGENTS.md gets the instruction? (a) Global AGENTS_GLOBAL.md — affects every session in every project, most representative; (b) SorraAgents project AGENTS.md only — contained blast radius." — Answer (user): "1. Global". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.
- Q2: "Measurement scope: (a) All sessions across all projects, or (b) only sessions in the project(s) whose AGENTS.md carries the instruction?" — Answer (user): "2. All (existing usage skill in the proxy will measure this)". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09. Note: intake could not locate a functional proxy usage skill — only `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` with no source files; AC 5 requires verifying that path or falling back to the repo analysis script.
- Q3: "Instruction fidelity: keep the literal sentence only, or append a short key-rule expansion?" — Answer (user): "3. Bare sentence". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.

## Assumptions recorded

- T0 = wall-clock time the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change lands on `dev` (commit time). Baseline = [T0−24h, T0). Experiment = [T0, T0+24h).
- "Previous period" = the immediately preceding 24h window (not same-weekday-matched). Day-of-week parity noted as a reporting nicety, not a requirement.
- Cost metrics used only where the log records `cost`; primary metric is `totalTokens` with input/output/cache breakdown as secondary.

# Intake Brief: Audit runner detects proxy 'cheap' mode and serializes parallelism

## Problem statement

The llm-manager proxy runs in one of two operating modes — **fast** (3-slot local
pool, cloud-backed) or **cheap** (reduced 1-slot local pool). The audit runner
(`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) currently ignores the proxy mode and always
uses its default parallelism (2), so during cheap-mode windows (01:00–10:00 local by
default schedule) an audit that launches concurrent pi child processes races the
single slot: degraded throughput, provider stalls, and concurrency-limit failures.
When multiple audits/dispatchers run at once the race is worse.

## Users

- Audit operators running `audit_runner.py` (item/project audits), and automated
  dispatchers (e.g. the herdr downtime worker's auto-audit dispatches).

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want the runner to automatically serialize
its pi calls when the proxy is in cheap mode, so my audits don't race the single
slot."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At runner start (`main()`, after arg parsing and before any pi call), the runner
   queries `GET <proxy-base>/admin/mode` with a short timeout and parses the JSON
   `mode` field.
2. When the mode is exactly `"cheap"` (case-sensitive), the runner sets **both**
   `AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1` **and** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` in its own environment
   for this run, and logs a clear detection line to stderr.
3. When the mode is anything else (including `"fast"`), or the query fails
   (unreachable / timeout / non-200 / unparseable), the runner **leaves all
   parallelism settings unchanged** (fail-open) and logs a warning; no verdict or
   status-lifecycle semantics change.
4. `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is renamed to `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` across code, tests,
   and docs; the legacy name is still honored as a fallback (new name wins).
5. New behavior is covered by unit tests (mocked mode responses: cheap → both env
   vars set to 1; fast → unchanged; query failure → unchanged and warning logged;
   legacy env alias still resolves). Full project test suite passes with the changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and
   `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` (rename references + new
   cheap-mode behavior described).

## Constraints

- **Read-only:** the runner may only `GET /admin/mode` — never `POST /admin/set-mode`
  (mode switching is operator/herdr territory; the audit mandate stays read-only).
- **Fail-open:** a mode-query failure must never break the audit or add more than the
  short timeout (≈3s) of latency, and must never change verdict semantics.
- **Per-process scope:** the change is `os.environ` on the runner process — it affects
  only this run's spawned pi subprocesses, not other processes or audits.
- **Host-wide semantics preserved:** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` keeps its host-wide
  flock-semaphore behavior; setting it to 1 in cheap mode caps *this run's* pi
  launches to one at a time (defensive — redundant with `AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1` but
  protects against sibling dispatchers sharing the same ceiling).
- Do not change verdict semantics, the two-phase pipeline, or the freshness gate.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py`:
  - `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` env (default 2) → `_resolve_phase2_parallelism()` —
    bounds Phase 1 child screening + Phase 2 child deep-analysis ThreadPoolExecutor
    concurrency (parent call never parallelized).
  - `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env / `--max-concurrency` CLI (default 5) →
    `_acquire_audit_slot()` — host-wide concurrent-pi ceiling via the shared flock
    semaphore (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`, `ENV_MAX_WORKERS =
    "AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY"`); saturated → fail-fast `unmet` unless
    `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` set.
  - `main()` (line ~5706) already wires `--max-concurrency` into `os.environ` before
    dispatch — natural insertion point for the mode query.
- llm-manager proxy (local checkout updated to `dev`, 72a0932; live at
  `http://192.168.0.199:8000`):
  - `GET /admin/mode` → `{"mode": "fast"}` or `{"mode": "cheap"}` (`mode.py`:
    `VALID_MODES = (fast, cheap)`, default fast, persisted in `proxy/.mode`).
  - `POST /admin/set-mode` exists but is out of scope (read-only).
  - Default schedule: cheap 01:00–10:00 local, fast otherwise; manual switches honored
    until next transition.

## Desired change

1. **Rename:** `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` everywhere
   (constant `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM_ENV`), keeping the
   legacy env name as a fallback alias (new name wins; legacy used only when new is
   unset). Update tests + docs.
2. **Mode query at start:** in `main()`, after arg parsing / `--max-concurrency`
   wiring and before command dispatch:
   - Resolve the proxy base URL — new `AUDIT_PROXY_BASE_URL` env var, default
     `http://192.168.0.199:8000` (matches pi's `models.json` "Local Proxy" baseUrl).
   - `GET <base>/admin/mode` with ≈3s timeout; parse `{"mode": ...}`.
   - If mode == `"cheap"`: set `os.environ[AUDIT_PARALLELISM] = "1"` and
     `os.environ[ENV_MAX_WORKERS] = "1"`; print a detection line to stderr.
   - Else (other mode / failure / timeout / non-200 / unparseable): print a warning
     (only on failure) and continue — settings unchanged.
3. **Tests:** mock the mode endpoint (monkeypatch the HTTP client or inject the base
   URL) covering cheap / fast / failure cases; verify env mutation and log lines;
   add a legacy-alias resolution test.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `main()` (mode query + env wiring),
  `_resolve_phase2_parallelism()` + `AUDIT_*_PARALLELISM_ENV` constants (rename +
  legacy alias)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — parallelism resolver tests (rename),
  new mode-query tests (mocked HTTP)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Concurrency / Parallel child deep analysis
  sections (rename + cheap-mode behavior)
- `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` — rename references
- Reference (external, read-only): `~/projects/llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
  + `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — `/admin/mode` contract

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (completed) —
  notes parallel-Phase-1 was dropped for local-model concurrency limits; same
  concern.
- `SA-0MSAIXTMS003REBW` — Phase 2: parallelize independent child deep-analysis calls
  (P3) (completed) — introduced the parallelism being gated here.
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 2 perf treatment applied to Phase 1 (P7) (completed)
  — Phase 1 child screening also uses this parallelism.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Phase 2 performance evaluation (completed) — flags provider
  concurrency limits for parallel child calls against the local proxy.
- `SA-0MSKB697P000T3HG` — Audit skill: tiered Phase 1 model (fast/cheap model for
  Phase 1 screening) (open, medium) — related cheap-mode theme; separate scope.
- `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY` — Implement or remove the unimplemented Pre-flight affirmation
  (open, high) — concurrent-audit guard; related, separate scope.
- `SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM` — Fix hardcoded DEFAULT_MODEL 'Proxy/qwen3' in audit runner
  (completed) — proxy model wiring in the runner.
- llm-manager: `LP-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N` (cheap mode keeps remote models enabled),
  `LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6` (mode.py) — the proxy-side mode feature this item consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — base URL default:** `AUDIT_PROXY_BASE_URL` defaults to
  `http://192.168.0.199:8000`, matching pi's `models.json` "Local Proxy" entry. If
  the proxy address changes, set the env var (no code change).
- **Assumption — exact match:** mode comparison is exact, case-sensitive `"cheap"`,
  per the request ("If it is anything else leave unchanged").
- **Assumption — fail-open:** a query failure never blocks or alters the audit —
  documented in AC 3.
- **Risk — rename breakage:** external scripts/herdr may set the legacy
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`; the fallback alias mitigates. Residual risk: a tool
  that *reads* the env name (none known).
- **Risk — stale mode during run:** the mode can change (or the proxy restart during
  a switch) mid-audit; the runner only checks at start. Accepted — a run sees one
  snapshot; the proxy restart semantics already tell clients to retry.
- **Scope-creep guard:** mode *switching* (`POST /admin/set-mode`), per-call mode
  re-checking, and the tiered cheap model (SA-0MSKB697P000T3HG) are explicitly out
  of scope; record as separate work items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: How should the runner determine the proxy's current mode? (I found no mode
  endpoint in the older checkout; `/v1/mode` was a 503 catch-all.)
  — Answer (user): `GET /admin/mode`. Source: interactive reply; verified live
  (`{"mode":"fast"}`) and in llm-manager `dev` (handlers.py, mode.py).
- Q: What does `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` do exactly? (Explained: host-wide per-pi-launch
  ceiling via shared flock semaphore, default 5, fail-fast on saturation.) Should
  cheap mode also set it?
  — Answer (user): yes, also set `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: If the mode query fails (unreachable/timeout/unparseable), leave unchanged?
  — Answer (user): OK (fail-open confirmed). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Rename `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` → `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` — keep legacy name as
  fallback or hard-break?
  — Answer (user): rename everywhere, fallback alias OK. Source: interactive reply.
  Research: refs in `audit_runner.py` (5), `test_audit_runner.py` (8),
  `audit-skill-reference.md` (2), `audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md` (2);
  SKILL.md has no name references.

# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — the item's title + description (the description contains the ACs and
   the Key Files section, so `key_files` may remain in the payload as a
   deterministic derivative of it). The per-path git components (committed HEAD
   blob hashes, working-tree state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are
   **removed** from the fingerprint — **no git calls in the computation**
   (`_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` are no longer used by
   the fingerprint). *(Producer decision 2026-10-21: proceed with the strict
   formula — recorded below.)*
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate
   a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test:
   fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored
   audit — **including changes to files the item itself touched** (stricter than
   the current per-touched-path formula). Regression test: fingerprint is stable
   across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences and
   across touched-file edits.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files
   section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing
   description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do
   **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content). This
   also removes the current comment-recorded-commit-hash contribution to the
   touched set (SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L) — the fingerprint must not depend on comments.
6. **Migration of legacy reports:** reports persisted before this change carry
   fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formulas that cannot be recomputed.
   Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`)
   so legacy/unversioned lines are distinguishable; legacy/unversioned reports
   fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt +
   `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`, plus the persist-write tolerance) — **no
   silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the
   one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after
   the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: after the simplification, remove the fingerprints-only
   git machinery no longer referenced elsewhere (verify each of
   `_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` — those still used by
   the file-scope manifest and Phase 2 remain). `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
   (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ) is **already removed**; `_resolve_audited_head` stays
   (still used by green-run attestation).
8. **Test migration (nothing silently dropped):** the existing per-touched-path
   invalidation tests (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change`,
   `..._dirty`, `..._staged`, `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`, the
   comment-contribution tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`) are
   rewritten to assert the **new rule** rather than deleted; new/updated tests
   cover title-change invalidation, stability across touched-file edits, and the
   versioned-line legacy fallback to the time gate.
9. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate
   section, currently ~lines 248-318/579-594/699/816), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
   (~lines 42/182-186/204-210), and the code docstrings on
   `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` /
   `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. All fingerprint call sites that must keep
   working with the simplified formula: `_check_audit_freshness` (item gate),
   `_get_child_audit_verdict` + `_child_content_changed` (child reuse, LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR),
   `cmd_check_freshness` (read-only probe, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI),
   `_run_remediation_loop` (ruff-config re-hash), `_phase_fetch_and_cq`,
   `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`, `_phase_children` (child audit persistence).
   **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes** — code
   comments/docstrings, README, and any wiki or docs-site entries that describe
   the freshness gate. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is
  reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the
  gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make
  any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still
  short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved); the read-only
  `check-freshness` probe and `isAuditFresh` (ship, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI) keep
  working.
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls
  through to a full re-audit (existing behaviour).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse uses the same fingerprint — it must keep
  working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2412) — payload =
    `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (per-touched-path, SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P).
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~1950) — content gate primary; time gate
    (60 s + persist-write tolerance ~30 s) floor for fingerprint-less legacy
    reports; persistence-write tolerance covers the runner's own writes
    (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
  - `_extract_content_fingerprint` (line ~2073) — parses the unversioned line.
  - `_resolve_touched_files` (line ~2213), `_compute_path_fingerprints`
    (line ~2336) — the per-touched-path git machinery this item's strict rule
    removes from the fingerprint (verify remaining uses: file-scope manifest at
    ~5224/7964/10897).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line ~1112,
    unversioned); embedded at ~5721/5747/6172 (persist) + re-extracted by the gate.
  - Call sites of the fingerprint: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020),
    `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_child_content_changed` (~7009),
    `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120), `_phase_gate` (~9466),
    `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357),
    `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11380/11516/11918).
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` — **already removed** (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ
    component replaced by per-path state); `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) stays.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — tests split across files; fingerprint/freshness coverage
  lives mainly in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (1336 lines:
  `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~190, `TestContentFreshnessGate` ~348 — incl.
  `test_fingerprint_payload_keys_exclude_global_head`, touched-file invalidation
  tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`, comment-hash tests) and
  `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`. Some existing tests assert the
  per-touched-path invalidation behaviour that this item reverses
  (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` /
  `..._dirty` / `..._staged`, tool-artefact invalidation, comment-contribution
  tests, `test_child_content_changed_fresh_survives_unrelated_head_movement` —
  these must be updated to the new rule).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section ~lines 248-254
  (content gate + time gate + fail-open), 292/309-318 (child reuse), 579/594
  (inherited pass / child reuse), 699/816 (Phase 2 child reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary ~lines 42, 182-186, 204-210.
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side
  `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based
  `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this;
  covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog). The ship-side
  `isAuditFresh` consumption is SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI (done) and stays in scope
  only as a consumer that must keep working.

## Desired change

Change `_compute_content_fingerprint` to hash only the work item's own data —
`{title, description_hash}` (Key Files parse from the description; explicitly
admit `key_files` in the payload or rely on `description_hash` as the ACs allow)
— with a versioned fingerprint line so legacy unversioned reports fall back to
the time-gate floor. Remove the per-path git components and the now-unused git
machinery from the fingerprint path; keep `_resolve_audited_head` for green-run
attestation; keep every consumer (item gate, child reuse, read-only probe,
remediation re-hash, child persistence) working against the simplified formula.
Update the fingerprint/freshness tests and both docs files to the new rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`
  (simplify to item-data-only), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_extract_content_fingerprint`
  (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, dead-git-
  machinery removal, docstrings
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — update
  fingerprint/freshness tests to the new rule
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines

## Related work

- `SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P` — Audit freshness: re-audit only when files touched by
  the work item changed (**done**, 2026-09-28) — implemented the per-touched-path
  formula currently in the code; this item's strict rule goes further (item-data-
  only, zero git). **The original observed failure is already fixed by this item.**
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content
  fingerprint (**done**, not in_review as the original brief stated) — the
  whole-repo working-tree component this item's rule REMOVES (superseded; the
  per-path state it inspired is also removed by this strict rule).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (**done**) —
  introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L` — Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments
  (**done**, 2026-10-21) — comment-recorded commit hashes feed the touched set;
  this item's rule removes the comment dependency (AC5).
- `SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI` — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (**done**) — read-only `check-freshness` probe consumer that must keep working.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (**done**) —
  the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item
  (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern,
  out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files
  section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content
  and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy/unversioned reports fall
  back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy
  item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a
  v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD/working-tree churn thereafter.
  Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence (now broader):** dropping the per-path git
  components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it — not
  just via another work item's Key-File edit, but **any committed or uncommitted
  change to a file this item touched** (the protection deliberately added by
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and kept by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, with tests asserting the
  invalidation). Accepted by design — producer confirmed option (a) on
  2026-10-21 (comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P); the audit's verdict remains the
  record for the item's own data.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the per-touched-path design re-touches the
  child-reuse gate, the read-only probe, and the ship-side `isAuditFresh`
  consumer. Keep those as consumers that must keep working — do not extend the
  item to re-design them.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for
  items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits
  ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit?
  — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to
  this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer:
  remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item
  supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per
  rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit
  decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the
  fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing
  time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

- Q (scope decision, 2026-10-21): The original trigger (unrelated whole-repo
  churn invalidating audits) was already fixed by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, so the

  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ. — Answer (Map, on behalf of producer): "a" — proceed
  with the strict item-data-only formula (title + description only, zero git
  calls), as originally recorded; per-touched-path invalidation tests are
  rewritten to the new rule. Source: comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P (reply to

  `_compute_content_fingerprint`/`_check_audit_freshness`/

  and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` are gone and the payload is

# Intake Draft — Audit: on ruff false positive, fix the ruff config and re-run (justified READ-ONLY break)

**Work item:** SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR
**Type:** feature | **Priority:** critical (operator-specified)

## Headline

When the audit's Phase 1 code-quality scan surfaces a ruff finding that a model-judged screen confidently identifies as a **false positive**, the audit applies a minimal ruff-config fix in the audited project, commits it (tracked by a newly created work item), re-hashes the content fingerprint, and re-runs only the code-quality scan. Uncertain findings are never auto-changed — they stay as findings annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required". This is an explicit, justified exception to the audit's READ-ONLY rule.

## Problem statement

The audit skill's Phase 1 code-quality check runs ruff over the scoped changed-file list and classifies findings by severity (`_classify_ruff`). False positives — findings that are not genuine problems (e.g. the EXE001 severity misclassification, SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P) — surface as critical/high findings that block closure and waste review cycles. Today each false positive is fixed once, manually, by editing the skill's severity map. There is no general mechanism for the audit to recognize a false positive, remediate it at the source (the project's ruff config), and re-verify.

## Users

- **Audit runner / release pipeline** — wants audits to converge without being blocked by non-issues, while never masking genuine findings.
- **Work-item producer** — wants visibility and control: no config change without a confident model judgment; doubt cases surfaced for producer decision; every config change tracked in its own work item with the commit.

### Example user stories

- *As the audit runner, when ruff flags a file with a rule that is a known misfire for that file, I want the audit to add a `per-file-ignore` to the project's ruff config and re-run the scan so the audit converges without a false blocking finding.*
- *As a producer, when the model is unsure whether a finding is a false positive, I want the finding retained and annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required" so nothing is changed without my confirmation.*
- *As a reviewer, when the audit applies a config change, I want it tracked in its own work item with the commit link so the change is visible and reviewable.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **False-positive screen:** ruff findings from the Phase 1 code-quality scan are classified by a model-judged screen into `genuine` / `confident-false-positive` / `uncertain`, each with a written justification recorded in the audit report. The screen errs on the side of caution.
2. **Confident remediation loop:** for `confident-false-positive` findings only, the audit applies a minimal ruff config change to the audited project (`per-file-ignores` or rule exclusion in `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml`; the file is created if none exists), commits it, **re-hashes the content fingerprint** (preventing freshness-gate invalidation from the dirty tree), and re-runs **only the code-quality scan** — the pipeline is not restarted. The loop is capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run.
3. **Uncertain findings untouched:** `uncertain` findings are never auto-changed; they remain findings annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required" and continue to block closure under the existing Phase-1 blocking rules (no config change, no commit).
4. **Tracked via a new work item:** each applied config change creates a separate work item (issue-type `chore`) linking the false-positive finding and the commit. The audit's existing prohibition on creating work items is relaxed **only after verifying** the runner's status lifecycle, persistence, and freshness-gate invariants are unaffected (verified by the audit skill test suite — lifecycle, phase1, freshness, core).
5. **Docs + green suite:** the audit SKILL.md (READ-ONLY safety section + the "Do NOT close, create, or delete work items" rule) and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the exception and the new behavior; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Ruff only** — eslint and other linters are out of scope for remediation.
- **Config only** — remediation modifies the audited project's ruff config; **no `# noqa` source edits**, no changes to the skill's own severity classifier map (classifier bugs like EXE001 continue to be fixed via normal work items).
- **Erring on the side of caution** — model applies a config fix only when confident; doubt → annotated finding, blocks as today.
- **Minimal, surgical config edits** — targeted at the flagged file(s), not sweeping rule changes; the config work item makes every change visible.
- **READ-ONLY exception scope** — the exception covers only: writing/creating the ruff config file, committing the config fix, creating the config-fix work item, and the code-quality re-run. All other audit phases remain read-only; the audit still does NOT close or delete work items, and never pushes (commit stays local; push follows the normal work-item workflow).
- **Lifecycle integrity** — the config-fix commit and work-item creation must not corrupt the audit's verdict-driven status lifecycle, persistence (readback verification), or freshness gate.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_phase_fetch_and_cq` runs the scoped code-quality scan: `run_code_quality(project_root=TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT, runner=runner, fix=False, files=cq_scope_files)` — read-only, scoped to the git changed-file list (SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58).
- Findings are severity-classified by `_classify_ruff` (prefix map in `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py`); critical/high findings block Phase 1 (blocking gate in `_decision_blocking_findings`).
- Audits are strictly read-only except explicit persistence and the automatic status lifecycle; SKILL.md: "Do NOT close, create, or delete work items during an audit."
- Ruff auto-fix (`run_ruff(fix=True)` → `--fix` → rescan, SA-0MQBQDLOY009EO4B) exists but fixes **code**, is not used by audits, and is not config remediation.
- Freshness gate fingerprints HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state (`git status --porcelain`); an uncommitted config edit would dirty the tree and change the fingerprint — hence commit + re-hash.

## Desired change

Insert a model-judged **false-positive screen** between the code-quality scan and the Phase-1 blocking decision. Screen output per ruff finding: `genuine` (keep, current behavior), `confident-false-positive` (propose + apply minimal config remediation, commit, create tracking work item, re-hash fingerprint, re-run code-quality scan only, capped at 3 iterations), `uncertain` (keep finding, annotate "candidate false positive — producer decision required"). Audit report shows the screen classifications and justifications.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (scan site), Phase-1 blocking gate, `_compute_content_fingerprint` (re-hash), status lifecycle; new false-positive screen + config-remediation + work-item-creation logic.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `run_ruff`, `_run_ruff_fix_mode`, `_classify_ruff`; possibly a helper for locating/editing the project's ruff config.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/code_quality.py` — `run_code_quality` orchestrator; may need to expose per-finding linter/rule detail for the screen.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — READ-ONLY safety section + no-create/delete rule → document the justified exception.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document the screen, remediation loop, and any new flags/env vars (e.g. iteration cap).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_phase1.py`, `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_core.py` — new tests for the screen, remediation loop, re-hash, work-item creation, and no-breakage verification.

## Related work

- **SA-0MQBQDLOY009EO4B** — "Add auto-fix support to ruff linter runner" (completed, high): ruff `--fix` + rescan machinery; foundation for fix-then-rescan, but code fixes, not config.
- **SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P** — "EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files" (completed): the motivating false-positive case; fixed once manually in the severity map.
- **SA-0MQA0SDW90056G6O** — "Linting & Severity Classification (Python/TS)" (completed): origin of the severity classifier this screen sits beside.
- **SA-0MQJONW3C007SZQY** — "Audit runner: manage work item status during audit execution" (completed): established the verdict-driven status lifecycle whose invariants must be verified unaffected before relaxing the no-create-work-item restriction (find-related automated report).
- **SA-0MSRLLQ0V008EW3J** — "audit_runner: warn/flag when zero ACs extracted instead of auto-approving" (open, medium): adjacent audit_runner robustness work, not a dependency.
- Automated find-related report (SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 shared lifecycle scripts, SA-0MSHTRS8F006RUDW Python 3.12 test-failure) — tangential; no impact.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** model proposes sweeping config changes → mitigated by minimal/surgical edits targeted at flagged files, a 3-iteration cap, and full visibility via the tracking work item + commit. Broader refactors are recorded as separate work items, not scope.
- **Over-remediation risk (masking genuine issues):** model over-applies "confident" → mitigated by caution-first instruction, mandatory per-finding justification, cap, and producer review of the tracking work item.
- **No-breakage risk (relaxing no-create-work-item):** work-item creation during audit could interact with lifecycle/persistence/freshness invariants → verified before relaxing (user requirement), covered by the audit test suite.
- **Freshness-gate risk:** config edit dirties the tree → commit + re-hash restores a stable fingerprint.
- **Cost/latency risk:** the false-positive screen adds one Phase-1 Pi call per audit; bounded by the existing per-call budgets and skipped when the scan yields no ruff findings.
- **Assumption:** default remediation cap = 3 config-fix iterations per audit run (configurable).
- **Assumption:** the config-fix commit is local (no push); pushing follows the standard work-item workflow once the config work item is processed.
- **Assumption:** `per-file-ignores` and rule exclusions are the only remediation primitives; severity-map changes to the skill's classifier remain normal work items (EXE001 pattern).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Who determines "false positive"?** — Answer (rgardler): "model judgement, erring on the side of caution, ask producer if in doubt". Final: a model-judged screen classifies findings; caution-first; doubt → producer decision. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: What does "fix the config" concretely modify?** — Answer (rgardler): "(a) the audited project's ruff config". Final: `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml` `per-file-ignores` / rule exclusion only; no `# noqa`, no skill-side classifier changes. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Re-run scope and lifecycle?** — Answer (rgardler): "code-quality, but commit and re-hash to prevent invalidation". Final: re-run only the code-quality scan; commit the config fix; recompute the content fingerprint so the freshness gate is stable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: "Ask the producer" in an unattended runner?** — Answer (rgardler): "(b) model only applies a config fix when confident; doubt-cases reported as findings annotated 'candidate false positive — producer decision required' (no config change, blocks as today)". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: Commit hygiene / work-item association?** — Answer (rgardler): "separate item — audits should NOT be forbidden from creating work items, relax that restriction (verifying it doesn't break anything first)". Final: audit creates a `chore` work item per config change; the no-create restriction is relaxed after no-breakage verification. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6: Config-edit scope (no config file present)?** — Answer (rgardler): "yes, create if needed". Final: the audit may create `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml` (or the `[tool.ruff]` section) in the audited project when absent. Source: interactive reply.
- **Issue type / priority (inferred, not asked):** `feature` (net-new audit capability) / `critical` (operator-specified via `--priority critical`).
### Planning session (Plan skill, 2026-08-14)

- **Q7 (remediation scope):** Should config remediation apply to blocking (critical/high) findings only, or to any ruff finding classified confident-false-positive? — Answer (rgardler): "(a) blocking findings only — **work item created for the medium and low pri**". Final: remediation = blocking-severity confident-false-positives only; medium/low confident-false-positives are classified, reported, AND tracked via a chore work item (no config change, no commit link). Source: plan interview reply.
- **Q8 (cap exhaustion):** After the 3-iteration cap, if a finding persists, should it remain a blocking genuine finding or be downgraded? — Answer (rgardler): "(a)". Final: remains a blocking `genuine` finding annotated "remediation loop exhausted". Source: plan interview reply.
- **Q9 (AC4 no-breakage ordering):** Test-first structure confirmed — verification tests (lifecycle/phase1/freshness/core suites) written and green while the no-create restriction is still in force; relaxation lands only with the work-item-creation feature; `wl create` reuses the runner's `_run_wl` with `--worklog-dir` resolution. Answer (rgardler): "confirm". Final: as stated. Source: plan interview reply.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-14 — Planned by `plan` skill: created 7 child work items (test-first) in 4 vertical slices (Screen → Remediation loop → Tracking+relaxation → Docs+green suite); added dependency edges T1→F1, T2→F2, F1→F2, T3→F3, F2→F3, F3→D1; appended Q7–Q9 to the Appendix. Children: Tests: false-positive screen (SA-0MST01NPD007MYG4), False-positive screen (SA-0MST01O4G002VPBR), Tests: config remediation loop (SA-0MST01OIN008MXYT), Config remediation loop (SA-0MST01OX4007Z17C), Tests: no-breakage + chore items (SA-0MST01PBJ008100Y), Work-item creation + no-create relaxation (SA-0MST01PQQ009T0CI), Docs + green suite (SA-0MST01Q4W005G495).

# Intake Brief — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H)

## Problem Statement

When the audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) completes an audit with a "Ready to close: Yes" verdict, it advances the item to `completed`/`in_review` but does **not** set the `needsProducerReview` flag. The producer-review gate (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in the ship skill skips items with `needsProducerReview: true`) is therefore bypassed for auto-audited items. However, the flag should only be set for **top-level** items (no parent): child items are covered by their parent's producer review, and marking every child for review would flood the producer queue with redundant approvals. The previous blanket behavior (set the flag for all items, SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW) was dropped during a later refactor (SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM), so this item restores the gating with the top-level-only refinement.

## Users

- **Producers / maintainers** — need assurance that every top-level completed work item proceeds to release only after their explicit review, without being buried by redundant child-item review requests.
- **AI agents running audits** — currently produce `completed` status without the `needsProducerReview` flag, creating a gap in the release gating chain for top-level items.

### User Stories

- **As a** Producer, **I want** every top-level item that an automated audit marks as "ready to close" to also have `needsProducerReview: true`, **so that** I can review it before release.
- **As a** Producer, **I want** child items to be **excluded** from the producer-review flag, **so that** I only review top-level items (their parent's review covers the subtree).
- **As an** AI agent running `/skill:audit`, **I want** the audit runner to set `--needs-producer-review yes` only when the item has no parent, **so that** release gating is enforced without queue flooding.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1**: When `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` in `audit_runner.py` applies a "yes" verdict (`status=completed`, `stage=in_review`) and the audited item has **no parent** (`parentId` is null/empty), the terminal `wl update` includes `--needs-producer-review yes`.
2. **AC2**: When the audited item **has a parent** (`parentId` set), the terminal `wl update` for a "yes" verdict does **not** include `--needs-producer-review` (the flag is left unchanged).
3. **AC3**: The "no" verdict and failure/restore branches never set `--needs-producer-review` (behavior unchanged).
4. **AC4**: Unit tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` verify both cases (top-level sets the flag; child does not), and the full audit test suite passes with no regressions.
5. **AC5**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (Status Lifecycle section) and code comments.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The change is localized to the standalone audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) — the AMPA engine's audit handler (separate code path, `docs/triage-audit.md`) is unaffected.
- Backward compatibility: the "no" and failure/restore paths must behave exactly as before.
- The flag must be set **only** on a genuine "Yes" verdict for top-level items — never on failure/fallback runs.
- No modifications to `.pi/` or agent-infrastructure directories outside the SorraAgents repo.

## Existing State

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (circa line 6740–6790): the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch builds `["wl", "update", <id>, "--status", "completed", "--stage", "in_review", "--json"]` — no `--needs-producer-review` flag is ever passed. (The flag was added by SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW but dropped in commit `3c876e1e`, SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM.)
- `ctx.wi` (the work item dict captured via `wl show <id> --json` in `_phase_gate`) includes `parentId` — `None` for top-level items, the parent's id for children.
- `wl update` CLI supports `--needs-producer-review <true|false>` (confirmed via `wl update --help`).
- Tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` assert the exact terminal `wl update` command; the mock runner returns a `workItem` without `parentId` (treated as top-level), so existing "yes" tests will need the flag expectation added.

## Desired Change

1. **`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`** — In `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, in the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch, when `ctx.wi.get("parentId")` is falsy (top-level item), append `--needs-producer-review yes` to the `restore_cmd` (both the `done`-stage and normal `in_review` variants). When the item has a parent, leave the command unchanged.
2. **Tests** — Update `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` "yes"-verdict tests to expect `--needs-producer-review yes` (top-level default), and add a test where the mock work item has a `parentId` asserting the flag is absent.
3. **Docs** — Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` Status Lifecycle section (bullet + Manual Fallback commands) to note that a "Yes" verdict also sets `needsProducerReview` for top-level items only.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (Phase 6, `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch, ~line 6770). Needs a parent check (`ctx.wi.get("parentId")`) before appending `--needs-producer-review yes`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — `TestVerdictDrivenStatusLifecycle`; `_make_runner` helper (add optional `parent_id`), and the three "yes" tests plus a new child-item test.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle section (line ~35) documents the `Yes` → `completed`/`in_review` transition; add the producer-review note.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

1. **Gate regressions:** If the flag is accidentally set for child items (or missed for top-level), the release gate either blocks release with redundant reviews or lets top-level items ship unreviewed. **Mitigation:** unit tests cover both branches explicitly; the change is a single conditional append.
2. **Scope creep:** The intent is strictly the audit runner's terminal transition. Extending the flag semantics to the AMPA engine, `persist_audit.py`, or batch skills is out of scope. **Mitigation:** keep the change localized; file separate work items for any follow-ups.
3. **`parentId` availability:** If `ctx.wi` were ever absent/empty, the check must default to top-level (set the flag) rather than silently skipping it. **Mitigation:** treat a missing/empty `parentId` as top-level (falsy check).

### Assumptions

- "Top-level item" = `parentId` is `null`/empty in the work item JSON — confirmed present on `wl show <id> --json` output.
- Child items' `needsProducerReview` flag is left **unchanged** (not force-cleared): the requirement says only that the marking happens "IF and only if" the item is top-level. A child already flagged (e.g., by AMPA) keeps its flag.
- The AMPA engine's `close_with_audit` handler already sets `--needs-producer-review true` via a separate code path and is unaffected by this change.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** (completed) — "Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks item as ready to close": the original blanket implementation, later dropped in SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM; this item restores it with the top-level-only refinement.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPG003OFYO** (completed) — "Filter closeWorkItemsAfterRelease by needsProducerReview": the downstream gate that this flag feeds.
- **SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS** (completed) — "Close work items after release only when readyToClose and producerReview conditions are met": release-time gating semantics.
- **SA-0MSAWFTZX003T042** (completed) — "Audit completion must set status: open (readyToClose: no) or completed (readyToClose: yes)": the verdict-driven lifecycle this change extends.
- **SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM** (completed) — "Fix hardcoded DEFAULT_MODEL 'Proxy/qwen3' in audit runner": the refactor (commit `3c876e1e`) that dropped the flag from the runner.
- **SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I** (completed) — "If a child audit is not ready to close then the parent must also be marked as not ready to close": parent/child audit consistency context.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Should child items get `--needs-producer-review no` explicitly, or be left unchanged?" — Answer (operator, via seed intent): "Marked as needing producer review IF, and only if, the item is a top level item". Interpretation: the flag is only ever set (to `yes`) for top-level items; child items are left untouched. Source: interactive request. Research: `wl update` supports an explicit flag, but force-clearing child flags could clobber flags set by other flows (e.g. AMPA) — documented as an assumption above.
- Q2: "Does this replace the previous blanket behavior from SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW?" — Answer (inferred from seed intent + git history): yes — the previous implementation set the flag for all items and was subsequently dropped; this item restores it with the top-level-only condition. Source: `git log -S needsProducerReview`, commit `3c876e1e`.

# Tests: false-positive screen (ruff findings)

Part of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR (Phase A — vertical slice 1). Test-first: this suite must be written and green BEFORE the screen implementation (F1).

## Goal

Prove the model-judged false-positive screen correctly classifies ruff findings from the Phase 1 code-quality scan into `genuine` / `confident-false-positive` / `uncertain`, records justifications in the audit report, and never triggers remediation for anything other than `confident-false-positive`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A batched Pi call over ruff findings parses into per-finding classifications; a finding missing from the batch response falls back to `uncertain` (caution-first), never `confident-false-positive`.
2. Unparseable/provider-error screen output (Pi model failure, timeout, concurrency-limit marker) degrades to `uncertain` for ALL findings — no remediation can be triggered from a failed screen (no config change, no commit, no work item).
3. The screen is skipped entirely (zero Pi calls) when the code-quality scan yields no ruff findings; non-ruff findings (eslint, etc.) are never sent to the screen.
4. Justifications are recorded per finding and appear in the audit report output for all three classifications.
5. Medium/low confident-false-positive findings are classified and reported but the screen never proposes config remediation for them (remediation is blocking-severity only — see F2/T2).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` (or a new `test_audit_runner_false_positive.py`) with mocked Pi calls asserting classification parse paths and fallbacks.
- Add report-content assertions (screen classifications + justifications present in the persisted report / `_build_issue_json` output).
- Add skip-when-no-ruff-findings coverage in the existing phase-1 scan tests.
- Keep tests green under the existing mocked-runner conventions in `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py`.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — existing Phase 1 scan tests to extend.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — report-output assertions may live here.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the screen under test (import target).
- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py` — shared mocked-runner fixtures.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; written before F1).

# Tests: config remediation loop (ruff)

Part of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR (Phase B — vertical slice 2). Test-first: this suite must be written and green BEFORE the remediation-loop implementation (F2).

## Goal

Prove the confident-false-positive remediation loop: minimal ruff config edit targeted at flagged files, local commit, content-fingerprint re-hash, code-quality-only re-run (pipeline not restarted), 3-iteration cap, and cap-exhaustion behavior — without ever touching `# noqa` source edits or the skill's severity classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Ruff config locating: `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff]` and `ruff.toml` are both located; a missing config file is created (per Q6: create if needed) — covered for both formats.
2. Remediation edits are minimal and surgical: `per-file-ignores` or rule exclusions targeted at the flagged file(s) only; no sweeping rule changes; no `# noqa`; no edits to `_RUFF_SEVERITY_MAP` / `_classify_ruff`.
3. Each applied config fix is committed locally (git commit; no push) and the content fingerprint (`_compute_content_fingerprint` incl. working-tree hash) is recomputed so the freshness gate is stable.
4. Re-run after remediation is scoped to the code-quality scan only (same scoped changed-file list, `fix=False`) — the audit pipeline is NOT restarted; remaining findings are re-classified.
5. The loop is capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run (default; env-configurable); a finding still persisting after cap exhaustion remains a blocking `genuine` finding annotated "remediation loop exhausted".
6. Uncertain findings never enter the loop (no config edit, no commit) — verified even when a remediation iteration is in progress.

## Minimal Implementation

- New test module `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` (or extend `test_audit_runner_phase1.py`) using the existing mocked-runner conventions.
- Mock git commit + fingerprint recompute; assert the fingerprint is recomputed AFTER the commit (working-tree clean).
- Assert re-run scope: only the code-quality call is re-invoked (no phase re-entry).
- Assert cap enforcement (0→1→2→3 iterations, then exhaustion annotation).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — new test module (primary).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — fingerprint invariants the re-hash must preserve.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_fetch_and_cq`, `_compute_content_fingerprint`, remediation loop under test.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — config-edit helper under test.
- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py` — shared fixtures.

## Dependencies

- F1 (the screen must exist — the loop consumes `confident-false-positive` classifications). Note: T2 is created before F2 but after F1 per the phase sequence; F2 depends on T2.

# Config remediation loop (ruff false positives)

Part of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR (Phase B — vertical slice 2). Implements the confident-false-positive remediation loop.

## Goal

For `confident-false-positive` ruff findings of blocking severity (critical/high) only: apply a minimal ruff config change to the audited project (create the config file/section if absent), commit it locally, re-hash the content fingerprint, and re-run ONLY the code-quality scan — capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run. Findings still present after the cap remain blocking `genuine` findings annotated "remediation loop exhausted". This is the explicit, justified exception to the audit's READ-ONLY rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Ruff config located or created: `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff]` section or `ruff.toml` (generic detection; created if none exists) in the audited project root (`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`).
2. Config edits are minimal and surgical: `per-file-ignores` / rule exclusions targeted at the flagged file(s); no sweeping changes; no `# noqa` source edits; no changes to the skill's severity classifier.
3. Each applied fix is committed locally via git (no push — pushing follows the normal work-item workflow) with a message referencing the work item; the content fingerprint is recomputed after the commit (working tree clean → freshness gate stable).
4. Re-run is scoped to the code-quality scan only (`run_code_quality(fix=False, files=<same scope>)`); the pipeline is not restarted; remaining findings flow back through the screen.
5. Loop capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run (default; env-configurable via e.g. `AUDIT_RUFF_CONFIG_FIX_CAP`); exhaustion leaves persisting findings blocking `genuine` with annotation "remediation loop exhausted".
6. `uncertain` and non-blocking (medium/low) findings never enter the loop; medium/low confident-false-positives are tracked via work items in F3 only.

## Minimal Implementation

- Config locate/edit helper (in `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` or a small sibling module): parse `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml`, add `[tool.ruff] lint.per-file-ignores` entries or rule exclusions for the flagged file(s), write back preserving other content.
- Loop in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` between scan and blocking gate: screen → remediate → commit → re-hash → re-scan (code-quality only), up to cap.
- Git commit via the runner's existing git execution paths (cwd-aware runner for sibling-project launches).
- Report output: per-iteration remediation notes (file, config change, commit sha, re-hash) in the audit report.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — remediation loop, commit, re-hash wiring.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — config locate/edit helper.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — READ-ONLY exception stub (full docs in D1).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — T2 suite the implementation must satisfy.

## Dependencies

- T2 (tests first — this item implements the behavior T2 specifies).
- F1 (screen classifications drive the loop).
