## Goal

Provide the agent framework with a shared, completion-aware wait helper so
agents stop burning sessions on fixed-length sleep polling of background jobs,
and give operators visible progress while a background process runs.

## Scope update (2026-10-18 reopen)

The helper core is **already delivered and committed to `dev`** (commit
`024194eb`): `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py`, 13 tests in
`skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py`, and a "Background job etiquette"
section in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`. A wiring audit then showed the helper
was referenced only by the implement skill; this item was reopened to roll
out the etiquette guidance and helper wiring across **all** skills and skill
scripts. The two children track that rollout:

- SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT — Roll out background-job etiquette guidance to all
  skills and global docs
- SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E — Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts where
  appropriate

The original scope ACs (core helper, tests, heartbeat, herdr reporting) were
satisfied by the delivered implementation; the open ACs below reflect the
reopened rollout scope. All original scope ACs are covered by the committed
helper and its tests.

## Justification (investigation findings)

Investigation of session `herdr-1792185693-133232-1304` (ran
`/skill:implement SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR`, an epic with 7 children):

- Session ran **23.7 hours** before intervention; it was still going when reviewed.
- **246 bash tool calls**, of which **95 were `sleep` calls totalling 21.0 hours —
  88.6% of the session was spent sleeping** (73 × `sleep 900`).
- **21 background processes** (`nohup`) were launched, each polled with the
  pattern `sleep 900; grep <log>; ps aux | grep` until completion.
- Pattern root cause: *fixed-length sleep polling is blind*. Each `sleep 900`
  is one turn — if the job finishes at minute 3 the agent still waits until
  minute 15 to discover it; if it stalls, the agent waits the full 15 minutes
  before deciding to retry. Every wake-up costs a full model round-trip
  (tokens, latency, context growth) and almost always returns "no change".
- Aggravating factors: heavy Local Proxy slot contention across ~12 concurrent
  herdr sessions made each audit take hours with repeated infra failures
  ("Connection error", "Script Execution Failure", stalls > 600 s, worklog lock
  contention), forcing re-launch/re-wait cycles.

## Out of scope

- The underlying Local Proxy slot-contention issue (separate infrastructure
  item) — better waiting cannot fix a serialised model slot.
- Fine-grained polling (`sleep 30`) as an alternative — that is *worse*
  (~2,400 round-trips over 20 h) and is explicitly an anti-pattern to avoid.

## Requirements (rollout scope)

1. **Shared/global documentation.** A canonical "background job etiquette"
   section in shared docs (referencing `wait_for_job.py`) that deprecates
   fixed `sleep N` polling of background processes, consistent with the
   implement skill section.
2. **Cross-skill rollout.** Every skill that launches or waits on background
   jobs (audit, ship, plan, test, …) and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` references the
   shared etiquette section at the relevant spots.
3. **Script wiring.** For each skill script that waits on a background
   subprocess/PR-status, record a decision (wire via `wait_for_job.py` or
   document "not appropriate"), and wire those marked appropriate so waits
   are completion-aware with timeout + heartbeat. Do not force integration
   where inappropriate.
4. **Behaviour parity.** Identical behaviour on environments without herdr env
   vars (helper silently degrades); existing tests still pass.
5. **Verification.** All tests pass via the test skill; docs and wiring
   committed and pushed to `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A shared/global doc exists that documents the background-job etiquette
  pattern and explicitly deprecates fixed `sleep N` polling of background
  processes, referenced from the skills that launch or wait on background
  jobs (audit, ship, plan, test, AGENTS_GLOBAL).
- AC2: Every skill/location listed in the rollout references the shared
  etiquette section where it launches or waits on background jobs (e.g. audit
  SKILL.md, ship SKILL.md, plan SKILL.md, test SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md).
- AC3: No skill doc recommends a bare fixed-length `sleep N` polling loop for
  background processes.
- AC4: A per-candidate decision is recorded (wired / not appropriate, with
  reason) for each script that waits on a background job; every candidate
  marked wired invokes the shared helper (grep- or import-verifiable).
- AC5: The implement skill section and the shared section are consistent
  (same helper and pattern).
- AC6: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to
  `dev`; item advanced to `in_review` once the rollout children are complete.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQUQZMWB0067UCR** – PlanAll: claim command fails due to stage/status validation in wl (completed)
- **SA-0MQ8NQNAR009BM8Q** – Ralph Loop skill should stop once ralph loop started (completed)
- **SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF** – Agent log review: global skill-improvement recommendations (2026-10-17 review) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+183 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msssnozn000lqkr, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+177 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+149 more)

data.description:
# Intake Brief — User-visible progress feedback in the Pi agent interface during long-running waits (wait_for_job)

## Problem statement

Operators running `wait_for_job.py` (e.g. `--pid <pid> --timeout 21600 --interval 120`) as a
bash tool call inside Pi report **no visible feedback in the Pi agent interface** while the
wait runs for hours. The wait helper already emits timestamped heartbeats to its own stdout
and (optionally) reports `working`/`blocked` to the herd sidebar, yet users are not seeing
these in practice — and there is no completion notification at all.

## Users

- **Operators / producers** watching a herdr pane or an interactive `pi` TUI while a long
  background job (audit, build, release, drive of epic children) is awaited.
  - *User story:* "As an operator watching a drive run wait for up to 8 hours, I want live
    progress visible in the interface I'm watching, and a notification when the wait finishes,
    so I don't have to guess whether the job is alive or silently stuck."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Live progress in the interactive TUI.** Running the wait as a bash tool call in an
   interactive `pi` TUI shows live heartbeats (elapsed / timeout) in the tool box, ticking as
   they stream — verified to work already and documented; the collapsed preview must make the
   heartbeat visible without manual expansion (or be expandable in one keypress).
2. **Sidebar status in headless/driven contexts.** When the wait runs in a context with no
   interactive TUI (driven child sessions, `pi -p --no-extensions`), the herd sidebar still
   shows live `working`/`blocked` status from `wait_for_job.py`'s `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` +
   `HERDR_PANE_ID` reporting. A **probe step** (during implementation, not a planning blocker)
   determines why an operator currently sees nothing: check whether the env vars are actually
   exported into the wait process on the operator's setup, and whether the herdr sidecar
   displays/receives `pane.report_agent` messages; then either fix the helper or document the
   explicit env-var requirement.
3. **Completion notification.** On wait completion (job done, timeout, or interruption) the
   user receives a visible/audible notification in addition to the log line — at minimum a
   terminal bell (`\a`) and a clearly formatted completion line; a desktop/notification-daemon
   firing (e.g. `notify-send` when available) is acceptable and non-breaking.
4. **Feedback documentation.** A short "background job etiquette / feedback" note documents
   which interface shows what: TUI heartbeats, sidebar status (env vars), and completion
   notification — including how to `tail -f` a heartbeat log in a pane.
5. **Testing.** Unit tests cover: heartbeat lines emitted at least once per poll interval;
   timer text; completion/timeout/interrupt paths; sidebar reporter payloads (working/blocked,
   correct `pane_id`/`source`/`seq`); and silent degradation without the env vars. Full project
   test suite passes with the new changes.
6. **Docs updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes (code comments, README,
   wiki/docs site entries) — the feedback note in AC 4 rolls into this.

7. **Live job output (extended scope, reopened 2026-10-18).** The helper shows what the
   watched process is actually doing, not just that it is alive. It auto-detects the job's
   output source — an explicit `--log FILE`, otherwise `/proc/<pid>/fd/1` (and `fd/2`) for a
   `--pid` wait when that resolves to a readable file — and emits a `output:` line naming the
   source it will tail. Output tailing is **ON BY DEFAULT**; `--no-tail` disables it.
8. **Incremental output, last 10 lines.** Each poll emits only the lines written since the
   previous poll (offset-based), capped at the last 10 (`--tail-lines N`, default 10). A poll
   with no new output must not re-print old lines. Rotation/truncation (size shrink) resets the
   offset instead of failing.
9. **Process vitals fallback.** Every poll emits one compact `progress:` line with process
   state, CPU time, RSS, thread count, child-process count and elapsed time, so a wait whose
   stdout is a pipe or socket (not retroactively readable) still shows liveness and a hint to
   pass `--log`.

## Constraints

- Must not break `wait_for_job.py`'s existing CLI surface (`--pid`/`--marker`/`--log`+`--pattern`,
  exit codes 0/1/2/130) — SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK contract.
- Silent degradation when herd env vars are absent must be preserved (fail-open, no crash).
- Completion notification must be non-blocking and fail-soft (no audible/desktop spam in
  headless automation).
- Driven children run `--no-extensions`, so pi-extension feedback channels are unavailable
  there; fixes must live in the helper (or its env-var reporting), not pi extensions.

## Existing state

- `wait_for_job.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/wait_for_job.py`, SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK) emits a
  timestamped heartbeat line to stdout ≥ once per poll interval, and a `HerdrReporter` that
  sends `pane.report_agent` (`working`/`blocked` + message) over the herd Unix socket when
  `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` and `HERDR_PANE_ID` are set (silently degraded otherwise).
- Pi's bash tool already streams partial output via `onUpdate` → `tool_execution_update`
  (100 ms throttle); the TUI renders a pending-tool box with a live "Elapsed" timer and the
  last 5 lines of partial output (expandable). Verified in pi bundle source.
- `herdr-agent-state.ts` (installed by herdr, `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`) reports pi's own
  `working`/`blocked`/`idle` to the sidebar, but only activates in TUI mode (`ctx.mode === "tui"`).

## Desired change

Improve the shared wait helper + docs so every feedback channel the user wants is real:
(1) TUI heartbeats — confirm/keep, make the preview show them without deep diving;
(2) sidebar status — diagnose the "nothing visible" case and make the env-var path robust and
documented; (3) a completion notification (terminal bell + `notify-send` when available).
Keep changes in the helper and its docs per Q3=b.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — heartbeat/timer text, completion notification (bell +
  optional `notify-send`), sidebar reporting robustness
- `skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py` — new unit tests
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — "Background Job Etiquette" feedback note
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts` — read-only reference (herdr-managed; do not edit)

## Related work

- **SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK** — "Background-job wait helper with progress heartbeat (completion-aware
  waiting)" — parent scope: the helper itself; this item is a follow-on on user-visible feedback.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill completion"
  (completed) — prior pane-status feedback work, useful reference.
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — "Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts where appropriate" (open) —
  follow-on rollout of the helper; feedback channels in this item should stay compatible.
- **SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT** — "Roll out background-job etiquette guidance to all skills and global
  docs" (open) — the AC 4 feedback note should feed this rollout rather than duplicate it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** "all feedback channels" (Q2) could pull in pi-extension work, notif-daemon
  plumbing, etc. Linked here as future work, not this item's scope — this item stays in the helper +
  docs (Q3=b). Extra channels beyond bell/notify-send are recorded as follow-up items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the interactive-TUI heartbeat channel already works and needs only confirmation +
  docs — if a probe shows it does not (e.g. collapsed preview hides heartbeats), the fix is in this
  item's scope (AC 1).
- **Assumption:** sidebar "working" may already reach the operator through herdr's own
  `herdr-agent-state.ts`; AC 2 scopes only what `wait_for_job.py` itself must guarantee, avoiding
  duplication.
- **Risk:** completion notification could disturb headless automation runs (bell chars in logs,
  notify-daemon calls). Mitigation: fail-soft, env-var-gated (`WAIT_NOTIFY=1` or equivalent), no
  crash if the notifier is absent.
- **Risk:** editing `herdr-agent-state.ts` is out of bounds (herdr-managed file); all changes stay in
  `skill/` files and docs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where do you watch the wait? (a) interactive pi TUI (b) herdr pane/sidebar (c) both (d) other" —
  Answer (user): "c — Both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What kind of feedback would satisfy you? (a) live TUI text, (b) sidebar status, (c) completion
  notification, (d) combination" — Answer (user): "all of those". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Scope? (a) investigate only, (b) improve wait_for_job.py + document, (c) general Pi feedback
  mechanism" — Answer (user): "b". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Is missing TUI feedback caused by waiting on a pre-existing PID not spawned by the wait script?" —
  Answer (verified by Map): "No. bash streams the wait script's own stdout regardless of the watched
  PID; ProcessMarker only probes /proc. Likely real causes: headless session (no TUI), sidebar-only
  viewing, or sparse 120 s heartbeats in a collapsed preview." Research: pi bundle source
  `dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-66G7ITPS.js` / `chunk-RH6M5TBT.js` (bash onUpdate → `tool_execution_update`,
  `toolTimerText`, `BASH_PREVIEW_LINES=5`), `wait_for_job.py` source, `herdr-agent-state.ts`.
- Q5 (plan): "Do you know whether the missing sidebar feedback is (a) env vars not exported into the
  wait process, or (b) a herdr-side display issue?" — Answer (user): "I have no idea". Final: the
  diagnostic becomes an in-implementation probe step (AC 2), not a planning blocker.

DISCOVERED-FROM:SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA. Investigation (SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 follow-on): the test semaphore bounds suite-LEVEL concurrency (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2) but ONE vitest suite spawns 15+ tinypool forks (SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 original cause; live evidence 2026-10-18: 7 x vitest/dist/workers/forks.js at ~74%% CPU each from a single suite, plus tinypool entry procs). Raising the suite ceiling without capping per-suite workers would INCREASE total load. Goal: cap vitest --poolOptions.forks.maxForks / tinypool maxThreads per suite so one suite stops consuming ~15 CPUs.

## Scope (producer-confirmed 2026-10-19)

**Scope 2 only — central test-skill plumbing in this repository.** The durable
fix lives in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` so every suite the test skill
executes (including `npm test` → vitest, and future consumer repos) is bounded
per invocation, instead of relying on each consumer's vitest config. Out of
scope: editing consumer-repo vitest configs (AI_Hell / TCE / ContextHub) —
those were capped separately under SA-0MSAK2ZH6009Z3TW and any remaining
per-repo caps are tracked there.

## Acceptance criteria

- `run_tests.py` injects `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` (default **4**) into the child
  environment of every suite command it executes, so any vitest invocation
  (direct or via `npm test`) is bounded to at most 4 workers per run. The
  command string is **not** rewritten, so the per-repo test-cache key is
  unchanged and read-only consumers (audit) still reuse entries.
- **Precedence:** an ambient `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` (operator/consumer-set) wins;
  the skill default applies only when it is unset. Values below 1 clamp to 1;
  non-numeric values warn and fall back to the default. Mirrors the
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` precedence/clamping contract.
- The injected value reaches a **real child process** (subprocess test reads
  `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`), and a pre-existing `NODE_OPTIONS` in the parent
  environment is preserved unchanged (vitest config/NODE_OPTIONS plumbing).
- Tests cover: default injection, ambient-value precedence, clamping, invalid
  fallback, and `NODE_OPTIONS` pass-through. No test spawns a real vitest run.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the cap, its precedence, the
  escape hatch, and that it is the per-suite complement to the host-wide
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` suite ceiling.
- Full project test suite passes (build → test → commit order).
- The empirical drain/load gate remains with the parent epic's measurement
  child (SA-0MVF792ST0036J5K); this item delivers the plumbing that makes that
  measurement reproducible across consumer suites.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — vitest worker-cap constants, resolver and
  env injection at the single suite-command execution point.
- `skill/test/tests/test_vitest_worker_cap.py` (new) — plumbing tests.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — cap documentation.
- `skill/test_runner.py` — env-scrub helper (read-only reference; not modified).
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — suite-level semaphore (read-only
  reference; not modified).

Priority: high — root cause of queuing and load saturation. Blocks: SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA full-suite gate and the TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY raise.

# Intake Brief — Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2→3 with mini-F7 validation

## Problem statement

`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 2` (in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) is an
uncalibrated first cut from SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG. Its sibling knob,
`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, was later right-sized empirically (F7 harness:
8 audits drain in 18.7 s at ceiling 3 vs 12.9 s at ceiling 6, batch-attributable
load delta ≤ 1.63, no swap growth — SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE). During peak multi-agent
traffic the test pool therefore queues more than the host requires, so agents
wait on the bounded test slot while CPUs remain idle. Raising the ceiling to 3
is only safe once per-suite worker pools are bounded
(`SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T`), otherwise more concurrent suites means more load, not
less queuing.

## Users

- **Operators / producers** running several agent sessions that finish with a
  test gate at the same time.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when three agents hit their test gate
    simultaneously, I want the third suite to start rather than wait up to
    `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (600 s), so wall-clock time-to-green drops without
    pushing the host into swap."
- **Agent sessions** (implement/audit/pre-push gates) that currently block on
  the bounded `"test"` semaphore slot.
  - *User story:* "As an agent, I want my test run to start promptly so I can
    complete build → test → commit without a long slot wait."
- **Maintainers** who need the ceiling to be an evidence-backed number rather
  than a guess.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer, I want the default justified by a
    reproducible measurement committed to the repo, matching the audit-knob
    precedent."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Default raised and documented in code.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` is `3` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; module docstring (line ~24), constant comment (line ~139) and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()` docstring (line ~1308) state the value and cite this work item. Precedence (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env > default) and clamping (values < 1 clamp to 1, invalid values warn and fall back) are unchanged.
- **Mini-F7 measurement gates the change.** An F7-style harness (see Key Files) runs **8 actual suite executions** through the real `run_tests.py` slot path (`--no-cache`, so cache hits cannot bypass the semaphore) at ceiling **3** and ceiling **2** on the 16-core host, sampling process counts, 1/5/15-min load and swap every ≤ 0.5 s via `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py`. Pass gate: batch-attributable load delta **< 4**, **no swap growth**, and 8-execution drain time at ceiling 3 **≤ 1.10 ×** the ceiling-2 drain time. Raw results are recorded in the work item (table) and as a committed JSON artifact (`docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json`). Reproduction commands: `python3 skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py --ceiling 2 --n 8 --out /tmp/ceiling-2.json` then the same with `--ceiling 3`.
- **Regression tests pass and the default is pinned.** All existing tests in `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` (17 test functions: 12 module-level + 5 class methods — the seed item's "10" is corrected here) pass unchanged, plus new tests: (a) the resolved default equals `3` with the calibration rationale, and (b) a cross-process run with **no** env override never exceeds 3 active slots. `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` passes unchanged (isolation contract, SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86).
- **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (env table `2`→`3`, the nested-run deadlock example that names "two concurrent full suites … `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`", and a short calibration subsection linking the measurement), `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` (or a new section documenting this run), and any other doc stating the old default.
- **Reproducible harness.** The harness is committed with a CLI (`--ceiling`, `--n`, `--out`), a per-batch isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, and unit tests covering its argument handling and report shape; the documented invocation reproduces the measurement.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new default (build → test → commit order per AGENTS.md).
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Ordering:** implementation must not merge before `SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T`
  (per-suite vitest/tinypool pools bounded) is complete; the measurement is
  only meaningful afterwards. This item is currently `blocked` on that item.
- **Measure attributable deltas, not absolute load.** The host usually carries
  unrelated agent traffic; the precedent (SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE) uses
  batch-attributable delta because absolute "load < 16" is not observable.
  Sample the baseline immediately before the batch and report both.
- **Do not change semantics:** bounded-wait, jitter (`TEST_LOCK_JITTER`), cache
  behaviour (hits never acquire a slot), the separate `"audit"`/`"audit-host"`
  namespaces, and the nested-run isolation contract stay as-is.
- **Do not relax nested-run isolation.** At default 3 the documented deadlock
  scenario shifts from two to three concurrent full suites; update the prose
  rather than weakening isolation. Replacing opt-in isolation is out of scope
  (SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF).
- **Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`** (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).
- The repo is the canonical source for `skill/`, so editing
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` is explicitly in scope for this item.

## Existing state

| Knob | Default | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | **2** | `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:138-139` | Uncalibrated first cut (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG) |
| `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 600 s | `run_tests.py:140-141` | Bounded wait for a free slot |
| `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` | 0.1 | `run_tests.py:145-146` | Per-waiter deadline stagger (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD) |
| `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | 6 | `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` | F7-calibrated precedent |
| F7 harness | — | `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` | Audit-only today: it launches `audit_runner.py issue` with a mock pi |
| Measurement tool | — | `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py` | Read-only process/load/swap sampler |

- The semaphore binds on **actual executions only**; `--summary`/cache hits
  never acquire a slot, so the harness must use `--no-cache` to produce real
  concurrency.
- This repository has **no vitest suites** (pytest + `node --test`); the
  per-suite worker fan-out fixed by the blocker lives in consumer repos
  (e.g. TCE). The harness therefore needs a deterministic synthetic suite
  payload (a `suiteCommands` entry in a throwaway repo that burns a bounded
  number of worker processes for a fixed duration), mirroring F7's mock-pi
  approach so the measurement is quick and non-intrusive.
- Docs stating the old default: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` lines 131,
  215. No literal default appears in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
  or `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Desired change

- Raise the default to 3 and make the rationale (calibration, blocker
  dependency, nested-isolation caveat) explicit at the constant and in the
  docstrings.
- Add a test-suite fan-out harness (F7-style, synthetic payload) that measures
  drain time, load delta and swap delta at ceilings 2 and 3, and commit the
  raw artifact.
- Update the test-skill reference (table, nested-deadlock example, calibration
  subsection) and the F7 validation report.
- Extend the semaphore test suite with the default-pinning and
  default-ceiling cross-process tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Raise `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` to 3;
  update module docstring, constant comment and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()`
  docstring with the calibrated value and citation.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — Add default-pinning test
  (resolved default == 3 with rationale) and a cross-process test proving the
  un-overridden default bounds concurrency to ≤ 3.
- `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` *(or a new sibling
  `skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py`)* — Add the test-suite ceiling mode:
  throwaway repo + `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`, N concurrent
  `run_tests.py --no-cache` executions, per-batch `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, sampler.
- `tests/test_validate_fanout.py` *(or the new harness's test module)* — Unit
  tests for harness argument handling, ceiling propagation and report shape.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Env table default, nested-run deadlock
  example, calibration subsection.
- `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` — Measurement method, results table,
  conclusion for the test ceiling.
- `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` *(new)* — Raw harness artifact
  (precedent: `docs/dev/audit-ceiling-validation.json`).
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — docstring only, and only if the
  harness cannot live in `validate_fanout.py` and needs the shared sampler
  contract restated (no code change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA` — discovery source (flags the uncalibrated default).
- `SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T` — **blocker**: bound per-suite vitest/tinypool worker
  pools; raising the ceiling is unsafe until this lands.
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — F7 calibration precedent for
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (method, metrics, doc layout to mirror).
- `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG` — introduced the test semaphore and the current
  default of 2.
- `SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD` — staggered bounded wait; semantics must be preserved.
- `SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86` — nested-run isolation; the deadlock example in the
  docs depends on the ceiling value.
- `SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO` — semaphore contention telemetry (open); supplies
  future evidence for further tuning beyond 3.
- `SA-0MVEDIUA80038VAQ` — single source of truth for audit/test timeout
  constants (open); coordinate if it moves these constants.
- `SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42` — migrates `validate_fanout._git` to the sandbox
  helper (open/blocked); potential same-file conflict if the harness is added
  to `validate_fanout.py`.
- `docs/dev/fanout-batch-validation.md`-style raw artifacts:
  `docs/dev/fanout-batch-validation.json`, `docs/dev/audit-ceiling-validation.json`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-subscription on small hosts.** A fixed default of 3 could add
  load on an 8-core host or a repo whose suite spawns many workers. Mitigation:
  the value is only raised after the blocker bounds per-suite pools; repos that
  must never overlap browser stages still set `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`
  (documented escape hatch).
- **Risk: synthetic payload does not represent real suites.** Mitigation:
  document what the harness models (suite-level concurrency through the real
  semaphore path with a bounded worker fan-out) and pair the measurement with
  the blocker's per-suite evidence; do not claim it proves per-suite behaviour.
- **Risk: flaky load measurements on a busy shared host.** Mitigation:
  attributable-delta method, repeated runs, and reporting the baseline; never
  gate on absolute load.
- **Risk: same-file conflict** with SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42 if the harness is added
  to `validate_fanout.py`. Mitigation: prefer a new sibling module or rebase
  after that item lands.
- **Scope-creep risk:** raising further (4+) or dynamically sizing by CPU count
  is **not** in scope; record as follow-up items instead.
- **Assumption (documented):** the 1.10 × drain-time bound in AC2 is the
  agent's proposal for "no wall-time regression beyond a measured bound"; the
  actual measured bound is recorded in the artifact and the brief is updated if
  the measurement justifies a different threshold.
- **Assumption:** "8 test-suite executions" means 8 concurrent
  `run_tests.py --no-cache` invocations against a fast synthetic suite, matching
  the F7 batch shape (N=8).
- **Assumption:** the 16-core host described in the seed item is the host the
  harness runs on; if it is unavailable, record the host's CPU count with the
  measurement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- The seed context (problem, rationale, dependency and four acceptance
  criteria) was sufficient to draft this brief, so no interview round was
  raised. Drafted from: the work-item description, the dependency
  `SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T`, the F7 precedent `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE`, and a repo
  search of the semaphore implementation, tests and docs.
- Research note — test inventory: `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py`
  contains 17 test functions (12 module-level, 5 class methods), not the "10"
  stated in the seed description. `test_default_ceiling` and
  `test_ceiling_from_env` assert against `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT`, so
  raising the constant does not break them; a new pinning test is still needed
  to prevent silent reversion.
- Research note — measurement feasibility: `run_tests.py` serves cache hits
  without acquiring a slot, so a naive harness would measure nothing; the
  harness must pass `--no-cache` (or `--force`). `validate_fanout.py` currently
  hardcodes `AUDIT_RUNNER` invocations but already provides the sampler,
  throwaway-worklog and per-batch `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` patterns to reuse.
- Research note — repository shape: this repo has no vitest suites (pytest +
  `node --test` only), so the per-suite worker fan-out addressed by the blocker
  lives in consumer repos; the harness needs a synthetic `suiteCommands`
  payload.
- Research note — duplicate check: searches for `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`,
  "test concurrency ceiling" and "fanout calibration" surfaced only related
  items (telemetry, constants SSOT, jitter, nested isolation) and no completed
  item that already raises this default. No duplicate work identified.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE** – Tune audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling to eliminate residual bounded-queue saturation (completed)
- **SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG** – Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive (completed)
- **SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB** – Investigate audit concurrency TimeoutError errors (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, 0muszjrb9006zche, acceptance, audit, audits (+56 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0muszjrb9006zche, acceptance, audit, audits, blocked (+52 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, audit, blocked, bound, bounded (+43 more)



## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19T12:04:43Z — plan skill decomposed this item into 7 children (2 test-first slices,
  harness, gating measurement, code change, docs, verification) and wired 10
  dependency edges. AC list markers in this brief and in the children were
  normalised from `1.` numbering to `- ` bullets so the shared tree-coverage
  review can machine-check parent→child AC coverage; each child also carries a
  "Parent ACn traceability" bullet. Coverage review: 100% (action `proceed`).

### Plan session (2026-10-19, plan skill)

- **No blocking interview round raised.** The intake brief already answers the
  plan-specific inputs (target outcome, definition of done, constraints, risky
  assumptions) for every proposed feature, so re-asking would duplicate
  recorded information (interview contract rule 1).
- Decisions taken from the brief and confirmed by the `/plan` invocation:
  1. *Harness location* — **new sibling module** `skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py`
     rather than extending `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py`. Evidence: brief
     §Desired change and the same-file conflict risk with
     SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42. Answering party: producer (brief) confirmed by the
     `/plan SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5` invocation.
  2. *No-regression threshold* — the AC2 **1.10 × drain-time** bound is kept as
     the gate, with the measured value reported in the artifact (brief
     §Risks & assumptions, documented assumption).
  3. *Ordering* — measurement and every mutation of the default stay after
     blocker SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T (brief §Constraints), expressed as a
     dependency edge on the measurement child.
- Q: "Should planning wait until SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T completes?" —
  Answer: no; decomposition, the test-first slices and the harness are

- OPEN QUESTION (producer, non-blocking): confirm the 1.10 × drain-time gate is

## Goal

Free up host-wide test-slot capacity so concurrent implement sessions stop queueing/timeouting on full-suite runs. Today `implement.py finish` runs the FULL suite twice per work item: once against the dirty worktree before commit (a cache-keyed result that no later consumer can ever reuse, because the pre-commit git-state fingerprint is unique, and because worktree runs cache in a different namespace from the main checkout), and again in the pre-push hook at the pushed commit. Each real full run holds one of only 2 host-wide "test" slots for the whole suite duration, so 3+ concurrent finishes saturate the ceiling and the 3rd times out (TestConcurrencyTimeout after TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600s).

Decision (operator-approved, Option A): run **changed-scope tests only during implementation**; the **full suite first runs at the dev-push integration gate** (pre-push hook — unchanged, still runs `--scope full` on pushes to dev/main). No batching of pushes. Release (dev→main) must still assert the main branch is full green after the merge and before the release is made. Applies to all repos via the framework (this repo is the canonical source; global install via install_pi.sh).

## Out of scope

- Batching pushes to dev (explicitly not desired by the operator).
- Changing the audit skill's read-only cache consumption or F3 auto-execution.
- Raising TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY / slot sizing (operator constraint: more slots → CPU-bound).
- Changed-scope selector accuracy improvements (unchanged).

## Requirements

1. `implement.py finish` stops running a `--scope full` suite before commit. Changed-scope validation (Step 3 + fix-and-re-run loop) remains the pre-commit gate.
2. The dev-push pre-push hook stays the single full-suite integration gate (`--scope full` on dev/main pushes), populating the main-checkout `.worklog/cache` that post-push verification and audits consume.
3. Post-push belt-and-suspenders verification becomes **read-only**: a `run_tests.py --summary` cache check that fails loudly only when no green full entry exists for HEAD (TTL expiry / missing run) — no suite execution for verification.
4. Release path (ship skill `pushToDev()` / `merge-dev-to-main.sh`) must assert the full suite is green after the dev→main merge and before the release; verify existing enforcement and add if missing.
5. Framework docs and global AGENTS guidance updated to describe the new regime consistently (implement SKILL.md, test SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, and any dev reference docs that describe the double-gate).
6. Existing tests updated to the new behaviour; all tests pass via the test skill.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: `implement.py finish` performs no `--scope full` suite run before commit; its report contains no full-scope test step. Verifiable via the finish report JSON (no `scope: "full"` attempt) and via implement-skill tests.
- AC2: The dev-push pre-push hook still runs the full suite (`--scope full`) for pushes to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` (unchanged enforcement — test/verifiable in the hook).
- AC3: Post-push belt-and-suspenders verification executes no suite command; it asserts a green cached full entry at HEAD and exits non-zero with an actionable message on a cache miss-verifiable by running the verification command and observing no suite execution (cache hit path).
- AC4: The release flow (dev→main merge) runs the full suite and blocks the release when it fails, on the merged main state before release.
- AC5: Scope-aware test documentation and the AGENTS global guidance no longer state that a full-suite gate runs before commit during implementation; they describe changed-scope validation during implementation and the full suite at dev-push integration (grep-verifiable: no `final full-suite gate before commit` language remains).
- AC6: All tests pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`); changes committed and pushed to `dev`.
- AC7: The audit skill consumes gate-produced full-suite evidence read-only: a green cached full run at the audited git state is accepted within the audit's own 24h acceptance window (`AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`) instead of the generic 2h, so the dev-push gate's evidence is reused (no F3 re-execution) for items pushed >2h earlier, re-audits, and HEAD-drifted audits; non-zero-exit entries still expire at the 5-min failed-run TTL (verifiable via test_audit_runner_green_run: green entry backdated 3h classified GREEN; same entry a miss under the generic 2h TTL).


## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/implement/SKILL.md
- skill/test/SKILL.md
- AGENTS_GLOBAL.md
- skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh
- skill/ship/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md
- tests/test_implement_run_tests_scope.py
- tests/test_test_skill_directory.py
- .githooks/pre-push
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py
- skill/audit/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md

## Goal

AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT (90s), AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (90s) and TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (600s) are each independently defined and tuned in their owning skill, with only a comment tying AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (=''matches AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT'') to AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. Tuning one budget (e.g. raising the audit queue timeout to survive deeper multi-agent queues) silently diverges from its documented twin, so the two host and queue budgets drift apart and the intended invariant (host wait stays inside the parent bash-tool ~120s execution timeout, queue admission stays inside it too) is only enforced by comments.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Shared timeout module**: a single source of truth for audit/test wait budgets lives in a shared module (e.g. skill/shared/wait_budgets.py or an extension of process_semaphore.py), consumed by both skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py and skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py.

3. **AC3 - Drift impossible**: the documented 'host timeout matches queue timeout / stays inside parent bash-tool timeout' invariant is enforced by the shared definition, not by a comment.
4. **AC4 - Docs**: audit-skill reference and test-skill reference point at the shared module for wait-budget tuning.

## Constraints

- Keep wait budgets configurable via env vars only (AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT, AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR); no config-file changes.
- Surgical change: audit/test concurrency semantics (priority queue, bounded wait, fail-fast on AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0, cache-hit bypass) are unchanged.

## Goal

The test skill's paced_runner() already accepts an on_wait callback (queued_at, wait_seconds) and implement.py logs a pacing line, but there is no structured, queryable record of how often suite runs wait on the test/audit semaphores, how long they wait, and how often the bounded wait expires (TestConcurrencyTimeout / audit timeout). Tuning TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY, TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT and AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT is therefore guesswork. Without telemetry the deadlock class tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF / SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 can regress invisibly.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Structured wait metrics**: every semaphore acquire wait on the 'test' and 'audit' namespaces (Semaphore.acquire in skill/shared/process_semaphore.py) records a structured event (name, max_workers, queued_at, acquired_at, wait_seconds, deadline_expired flag) to a stable JSON-lines location, e.g. a per-run or per-host file under a configurable directory.
2. **AC2 - Timeout events captured**: TestConcurrencyTimeout (run_tests.py) and audit timeout verdicts are recorded with the same schema (no new exceptions, no behaviour change).
3. **AC3 - Read-only aggregation**: a helper (e.g. skill/shared/contention_summary.py) aggregates the recorded events into a human/JSON summary (percentiles of wait, timeout counts, slot-saturation histogram) without acquiring any semaphore.
4. **AC4 - Documented tuning feedback**: docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md describe how to use the telemetry to tune the ceiling/timeout env vars; the full project test suite passes with the change.
5. **AC5 - Opt-out and boundedness**: telemetry is cheap (append-only, per-event timestamp), never blocks the acquire path, and can be disabled with an env var; tests run in temp dirs (PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation preserved).

## Constraints

- Recording must not add latency to the acquire path (no blocking I/O in the wait loop; write asynchronously or after the wait resolves).
- No behavioural change to concurrency semantics: ceiling, timeout, nested-run isolation and cache-hit bypass all unchanged.
- Respect PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation in tests so telemetry files never collide with the host-wide pool.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG - test skill shared concurrency primitive (defines ceiling/timeout)
- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF - multi-agent audit/test coordination (the deadlock class this telemetry makes observable)
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - nested-run semaphore isolation (PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR contract to honour in telemetry paths)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 - pacing telemetry (on_wait callback; existing partial hook)

## Goal

Nested-run isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) works only when a test fixture explicitly sets PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR to an isolated directory via nested_semaphore_dir(). Any NEW test that spawns a subprocess running run_tests.py (or invokes the runner in-process) silently re-enters the host-wide 'test' pool and can deadlock exactly as before: the outer run holds a slot the nested run waits behind until TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT. The LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE recursion marker already solves the analogous problem for the live-repo guard (subprocesses inherit it; nested guards stand down). The test semaphore has no equivalent, so the fix depends on every future test author remembering an opt-in convention.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Automatic isolation marker**: a run that holds a host-wide 'test' slot exports an inherited marker (e.g. TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD=1) to its subprocess environment; the marker is set/cleared by the same code that acquires/releases the slot (run_tests.py's _test_concurrency_slot), so it cannot drift from the real acquisition.
2. **AC2 - Nested runs auto-isolate**: when run_tests.py detects the marker already set (i.e. it is a nested invocation), it derives an isolated namespace automatically (e.g. a per-invocation directory under the marker's parent, or nested_semaphore_dir of a run-scoped root) instead of contending for the host-wide pool — no fixture opt-in required.
3. **AC3 - Explicit override still wins**: an explicitly-set PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR always takes precedence over the automatic derivation, so existing fixtures and operators keep full control.
4. **AC4 - Host-wide ceiling preserved**: top-level runs (marker absent) still bound themselves via TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY; only nested invocations isolate.
5. **AC5 - Regression test**: a test spawns a nested run_tests.py WITHOUT setting PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR while an outer slot is held, and asserts it completes without waiting on the host-wide pool (and that an explicit PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR still wins).
6. **AC6 - Docs**: docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/test-isolation.md document the automatic marker as the default contract (the fixture helper remains available); full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- The marker must be inherited by subprocesses only through the normal env chain — no global mutation of the parent's own environment (mirror the LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE pattern).
- Nested isolation must not weaken host-wide bounding for genuine parallel suites.
- Do not break existing fixtures that already set PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR explicitly (explicit wins).
- Full project test suite must pass.

## Related work

- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - introduced nested_semaphore_dir() + opt-in PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation (this item makes it the default)
- SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H / SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q - LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE recursion marker (the pattern to mirror)
- SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO - contention telemetry (complementary observability)
data.title: Automatic nested-run semaphore isolation: replace opt-in PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR convention with an inherited marker

## Goal

When TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) is saturated under multi-agent load, every waiting run_tests.py invocation polls the flock slot pool at a fixed 50ms cadence (Semaphore._RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS) with an identical 600s bounded wait. If several agents hit the saturated semaphore simultaneously (implement.py finish gates, the pre-push hook, audit F3 auto-execution all on the same host), they start their bounded waits in lockstep and, on expiry, all report failure at the same moment — creating a thundering-herd wave that re-enters together and re-storms the pool. The nested-run isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) removed the structural deadlock, but the lockstep wait/retry wave remains and makes the system look hung under sustained load.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Staggered wait entry**: waiters that start their bounded wait at the same time do not all poll in lockstep or time out in lockstep: the acquire loop introduces jitter (per-waiter random offset) into the retry cadence and/or the deadline so a herd of concurrent waiters desynchronises (e.g. jittered deadline within TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, or per-attempt jittered sleep).
2. **AC2 - Ceiling/timeout preserved**: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY still bounds concurrent executions and TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT still bounds the maximum wait; jitter only staggers, never extends the deadline beyond the configured bound. Cache-hit bypass unchanged.
3. **AC3 - Retry after expiry is not instant**: after a TestConcurrencyTimeout, callers (implement.py, pre-push hook path, audit F3) should not immediately storm the pool again — surface a guidance message with a suggested stagger (or a small built-in cooldown) so a herd does not re-enter in lockstep.
4. **AC4 - Deterministic tests**: unit tests assert (a) two concurrent waiters with different jitter offsets do not share the same deadline, (b) the deadline never exceeds TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT for any waiter, (c) a bounded wait still acquires when a slot frees (no starvation regression), (d) cache hits never wait. Tests must not rely on wall-clock sleeps where avoidable (inject time/random).
5. **AC5 - Nested-run isolation unchanged**: PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR/nested_semaphore_dir semantics are untouched; explicit PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR still wins.
6. **AC6 - Docs + full suite**: test-skill reference documents the staggered-wait contract; the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Jitter must be bounded (never extend the total wait past TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) and must not add meaningful latency to a cache hit or an uncontended acquire.
- Must not change the audit semaphore semantics (audit has its own AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0 fail-fast + bounded AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT path) unless trivially safe.
- Changing lockstep polling in skill/shared/process_semaphore.py affects the audit semaphore too — evaluate and either keep audit behaviour byte-identical or make the jitter opt-in per semaphore.
- Full project test suite must pass (build -> test -> commit order).

## Key Files

- skill/shared/process_semaphore.py
- skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py
- skill/test/tests/ (add staggered-wait tests near existing semaphore tests)
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (only for the retry-guidance message, if touched)
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md

## Notes on recent changes

- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 added nested_semaphore_dir()/PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation — validate the jitter change interacts correctly (nested runs use isolated namespaces; jitter applies per-namespace acquisition).
- SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE raised DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS 5->6 and made the audit ceiling right-sized — the test semaphore's TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 is unchanged; the herd is a TEST-semaphore phenomenon.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF - multi-agent audit/test coordination (parent class of the deadlock/starvation problem)
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - nested-run semaphore isolation (recent change to validate against)
- SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO - contention telemetry (makes the wave observable once implemented)
- SA-0MVEDIUA80038VAQ - shared timeout constant (would centralise the 600s bound this item jitters)

## Goal (discovered during SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD)

The per-repo test cache (skill/test_cache.py) dedupes *completed* runs at the same git state (2h TTL), but two agents that both miss the cache at the identical command + git state execute the full suite **concurrently** (both acquire a slot when TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY >= 2; the second duplicates work the first is already doing). With nested-run isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) now making the host-wide 'test' pool the only contention point, the next structural reduction is single-flight: the second caller should wait on the first in-flight run's result instead of acquiring its own slot and re-running.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - In-flight markers**: a run that misses the cache publishes an in-flight marker keyed by (normalized command, git state, scope, test_type) before executing and clears it on completion (including crash/timeout paths).
2. **AC2 - Coalescing**: a second caller that finds a fresh in-flight marker for the identical key waits for that run's stored result (bounded by TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) instead of executing a duplicate; if the marker goes stale (holder died) the caller proceeds normally.
3. **AC3 - No correctness change**: cache hits/stores/TTL/scope/test_type semantics are unchanged; a coalesced caller receives the identical result dict shape as a cache miss+run (with a marker such as coalesced: true) so downstream consumers are unaffected.
4. **AC4 - Bounded, no new deadlock**: coalescing never blocks past TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT and cannot deadlock (stale markers expire; a crashed holder is detectable by marker age/pid).
5. **AC5 - Tests**: deterministic tests cover (a) two callers with the same key execute once, (b) different keys still execute independently, (c) a stale marker does not block, (d) cache hits bypass coalescing.
6. **AC6 - Docs + full suite**: test-skill reference documents the coalescing contract; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken the two-slot host-wide ceiling (this reduces duplicate work, not the ceiling).
- Single-flight must be per-repo (and worktree-aware), honouring the existing git-state fingerprint.
- Full project test suite must pass (build -> test -> commit order).

## Related work

- SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD - staggered back-off (this item's parent discovery; complementary — stave off the herd, then coalesce its redundant members)
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - nested-run isolation (makes the top-level pool pure)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 - pacing telemetry (on_wait) - the coalesced wait should reuse it
- SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO - contention telemetry (observability for coalescing effectiveness)
data.title: Test cache: single-flight coalescing for identical in-flight suite runs

## Goal

Refine the audit stage's acceptance of full-suite evidence: matching-git-state GREEN cached entries are accepted **without a practical time bound** (code identity is already guaranteed by the git-state key), so audit re-runs never occur purely because evidence is old. Red entries keep the existing 5-minute failed-run expiry.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 shipped `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 24h` as the audit's acceptance window. The operator's challenge is valid: the full suite was proven green by the dev-push gate at the pushed commit; the cache key is the byte-identical git state, so the wall clock adds nothing about the CODE. Environment drift (deps/infra/host state) is the only thing a time bound hedges, and it is already caught fresh at the next dev-push and by the enforced ship release gate (AC4) before anything ships. A 24h expiry therefore causes needless F3 full-suite re-runs (slot contention) for re-audits, backlogs and HEAD-drifted audits with no safety gain.

## Requirements

1. Replace the 24h audit acceptance with a no-practical-bound semantics for GREEN entries (e.g. an explicitly documented large `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, or an explicit green-never-expires mode in the audit's lookup); non-zero-exit entries remain capped at the 5-minute failed-run TTL (`lookup()` already applies `min(ttl, FAILED_RUN_TTL_SECONDS)`).
2. Pin the semantics with tests: a green entry backdated well beyond 24h (e.g. 120 days) still classifies GREEN; a green entry beyond the generic 2h TTL is NOT a miss; a failed entry still expires at 5 minutes.
3. Update skill/audit/SKILL.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md (remove the "24h acceptance window" language).
4. F3 (auto-execute on genuine miss) and F4 (never-block) behaviour unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A green full-suite entry backdated 120 days at a matching git state classifies as AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN (no F3 execution).
- AC2: A failed (non-zero) entry still expires after the 5-minute TTL and is never accepted as evidence.
- AC3: Audit docs no longer describe a time-based acceptance window for green entries; they state green evidence at a matching git state is accepted without a practical time bound (grep-verifiable).
- AC4: All tests pass via the test skill (changed-scope and the audit test group); changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Audit: accept matching-state green full-suite evidence without a practical time bound

## Goal

Make the changed-scope test gate run the **union of all matching skill groups**, not a single arbitrary pick, and align the two selectors (implement.py `run_tests` and `run_tests.py --scope changed`) on the same semantics.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

`select_group_from_changed_files` returns the single group with the fewest commands; when multiple groups match with equal command counts, `min(matching, key=matching.get)` returns an arbitrary one (insertion order). A cross-skill change — e.g. touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` simultaneously, exactly like SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 — therefore gate-tests only ONE of the affected skill suites pre-commit, deferring the rest to the push-time full gate (and the import-graph selector cannot cover them: `map_changed_to_tests` only scans root `tests/`/`test/` dirs, not skill-group test dirs). The run_tests.py CLI's `--scope changed` uses a different (file-level) selector than implement.py's group-first selector, so the two agree only by accident.

## Requirements

1. A changed set matching N groups (e.g. implement + test + audit) runs the commands of ALL N groups exactly once (deduplicated), with each suite's cache key/type metadata preserved (`group:<name>`).
2. Matching-group selection becomes deterministic and documented (union by paths; no arbitrary single pick). When no group matches, behaviour falls back to the existing file-level selector / full suite unchanged.
3. implement.py `run_tests(scope="changed")` and `run_tests.py --scope changed` converge on the same group-union semantics (single source of truth for group selection).
4. Per-command timeouts account for N groups (a multi-group run must not blow the 600s default); cache entries remain distinct per group.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A change touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` invokes all three groups' suite commands in a `--scope changed` run.
- AC2: A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands).
- AC3: The CLI (`run_tests.py --scope changed`) and `implement.py` finish select the same command set for the same changed set (convergence test).
- AC4: No group match → existing fallback behaviour unchanged (file-level selection, then full).
- AC5: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Changed-scope gate: run the union of all matching test groups (fix single-group pick) and align selectors

## Goal

Unify the per-repo test-cache namespace across git worktrees and the main checkout so evidence produced in either checkout is reusable from the other (no duplicate full-suite runs at the same git state caused purely by the namespace split).

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

`test_cache.cache_dir()` resolves per checkout: a worktree looks for a worktree-local `.worklog` (created by `implement.py start`) → `<worktree>/.worklog/cache`, else `git rev-parse --git-dir`/`test-cache` — which for linked worktrees is `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>/test-cache`, a DIFFERENT namespace from the main checkout's `<main>/.worklog/cache`. Consequence: a changed-scope run cached inside a worktree is invisible to the pre-push hook / audit / belt-and-suspenders running from the main checkout and vice versa. Under the new regime (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81: full suite first runs at the dev-push gate in the main checkout), aligning the namespaces lets worktree gate evidence and main-checkout gate evidence share one store — eliminating a class of duplicate full runs and stale-miss F3/F5 auto-executions.

## Requirements

1. `cache_dir()` resolves a SINGLE namespace for a worktree and its main checkout — e.g. prefer the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` (resolve via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), or a shared `<git-common-dir>/test-cache`, falling back to the current rules for non-git/non-linked layouts.
2. Writes stay atomic (they already are: temp file + `os.replace`); concurrent writers from two checkouts must not corrupt entries.
3. Repos without worktrees keep the current behaviour byte-for-byte; the audit's read-only `query_cached()` and other consumers are unaffected API-wise.
4. Tests cover: a run cached in a worktree is a hit from the main checkout at the same git state (and vice versa); worktree-local `.worklog` presence no longer forks the namespace.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A suite cached from inside a linked worktree is served from the main checkout's `run_tests.py --summary` at the same git state, and the reverse direction also hits.
- AC2: A non-worktree repo (plain clone) resolves the cache exactly as today (byte-identical path resolution).
- AC3: 2 concurrent writers (worktree + main) at the same key leave a valid entry (no torn write).
- AC4: All tests pass via the test skill (test_cache suite + affected consumers); changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout

# Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g. `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
- **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
- **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
- **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.
- **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1 harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-21T15:12:22Z — plan skill decomposed this epic into 7 children (1 pre-existing task + 6 new
  features) and wired 11 dependency edges in test-first ordering (harness/baseline →
  concurrency ceiling + JSON re-asks + child-screen budget → Phase 1 call count →
  post-change verification → documentation). Parent AC markers were normalised from
  `1.` numbering to `- ` bullets and unwrapped to single lines so the shared
  tree-coverage review can machine-check parent→child AC coverage; each child carries
  a "Parent ACn traceability" bullet. Coverage review: 100% (action `proceed`).

## Goal

- Tests assert the JSON report shape: top-level keys `success` and `config` (`ceiling`, `n`, `suite_seconds`, `semaphore_dir`), plus `before`, `after`, `peak` (`processes`, `load`) and `batch` (`n`, `ok`, `elapsed_seconds`, `baseline_load`), and `results` with one `exit_code` entry per invocation.
- Tests assert the synthetic-payload contract: the throwaway repo contains `.pi/test-config.json` with a `suiteCommands` entry, and each batch uses an isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` inside that batch's directory (never the host-wide pool).

- The red step is recorded: a work-item comment notes the test module failing against the pre-harness tree (missing module/CLI), then passing once SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.2 lands.

Child of SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5 (Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2->3 with mini-F7 validation).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want a reproducible F7-style harness for the **test** semaphore, so the ceiling value is justified by a committed measurement instead of an uncalibrated guess (the audit knob's precedent, SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New module `skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py` with shebang and module docstring, CLI flags `--ceiling` (default 2), `--n` (default 8), `--out`, `--suite-seconds`, `--dry-run`; out-of-range values exit non-zero with a clear message.
- The harness builds a throwaway repo containing `.pi/test-config.json` with a `suiteCommands` entry whose synthetic payload burns a bounded number of worker processes for `--suite-seconds` and exits 0 (mirrors F7's mock-pi approach; no vitest, no browser).
- It launches N concurrent `run_tests.py --no-cache` invocations through the **real** semaphore path with `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=<ceiling>`, so cache hits cannot bypass the slot, and uses a per-batch isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` so the measurement reflects this batch only.
- It samples process counts and 1/5/15-min load and swap every <= 0.5 s via `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py`, and emits a JSON report with `config`, `before`, `after`, `peak`, `batch` (including `baseline_load` and `elapsed_seconds`) and per-invocation `results`.
- `--dry-run` prepares the throwaway repo and prints the report skeleton without launching suites; it is fast enough for unit tests.
- `python3 skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py --dry-run` and the documented invocation (`--ceiling 2 --n 8 --out /tmp/ceiling-2.json`) both succeed on this host.
- The unit tests from SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.1 pass unchanged (no test edits in this slice beyond making red green by satisfying the pinned contract).

- Parent AC2 traceability (harness half): an F7-style harness runs 8 actual suite executions through the real `run_tests.py` slot path (`--no-cache`), at ceiling 3 and ceiling 2, sampling process counts, 1/5/15-min load and swap every <= 0.5 s via `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py`.
- Parent AC5 traceability: reproducible harness — the harness is committed with a CLI (`--ceiling`, `--n`, `--out`), a per-batch isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, and unit tests covering its argument handling and report shape, so the documented invocation reproduces the measurement.

- New sibling module (do **not** extend `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py`, which is being migrated by SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42) reusing its patterns: throwaway git+worklog dir, `FanoutSampler`, `_git`, per-batch `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`.
- Synthetic payload: a small Python script in the throwaway repo spawned by the `suiteCommands` entry, forking a bounded number of workers (e.g. 4) for `--suite-seconds`, so suite-level concurrency is what is measured.
- Reuse `shared.measure_fanout.collect()` for before/after snapshots; summarise peak load/process counts.
- Report `baseline_load` (sampled immediately before launching) alongside peaks so deltas are batch-attributable.

## Key Files

## Deliverables

- Committed, CLI-driven harness with a documented reproduction command.
