# Ship gates accept versioned fingerprint line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As a release operator, I want the ship audit gates to recognise the new versioned content-fingerprint line, so the content-freshness fast path keeps working after the fingerprint is versioned.

**Context:** `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` mirrors the runner's prefix (`AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = 'Audit content fingerprint: '`) and detects fingerprint-bearing audits with `haystack.includes(...)` (~line 478) to decide whether to spawn the read-only `check-freshness` probe (`queryContentFreshness`, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI). Once the runner writes `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hex>`, that `includes()` check silently fails and every audited item falls back to the local time gate — fail-safe but a regression of the release fast path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` is updated to the versioned `'Audit content fingerprint (v2): '` (or `hasContentFingerprint` is made version-aware), so a v2-bearing audit is detected and the probe path is taken.
2. `hasContentFingerprint()` returns `false` for legacy unversioned (`Audit content fingerprint: <hex>`) reports — those correctly fall back to the local time gate instead of spawning a probe that would only reproduce the time gate — and `false` for fingerprint-less reports; `true` for v2 reports in both `audit.rawOutput` and `audit.summary`.
3. `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` covers v2-present, legacy-v1-present and absent cases, and the existing `check-final-validation.js` consumer (`classification.kind === 'stale' && hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`) still routes stale+v2 audits to the probe.
4. Ship unit tests for the audit gate pass via `/skill:test` (`tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-ship-scripts.mjs`).
5. Sequencing note recorded: this item should land in the same release as the fingerprint change; if it lands later, the intervening window is fail-safe (extra re-audits, no incorrect passes).

## Minimal implementation

- Update the mirrored prefix constant and `hasContentFingerprint()` (plus its docstring) in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` with the three cases.
- No change to `queryContentFreshness` / `audit-freshness.js` behaviour.

## Key Files

# Add a session-time-analysis skill ("where does Pi time go") and weave it into agent-log-review

## Summary
On 2026-10-21 an ad-hoc analysis of all 25 active Pi sessions in AI_Hell (00:52 to 18:54 local) answered the
operator question "where is the time going?": about 8.7 h of ~11.8 h active wall-clock was spent blocked in
wait_for_job.py (37 waits, avg ~15 min); one hung evaluate.mjs command burned 2.8 h; test runs ~1.4 h;
>96% of ~123 M tokens were cache reads. The analysis used throwaway scripts in /tmp/pi_time/
(analyse.py, deep.py, final.py, theme.py, content.py) which will not survive a reboot.

This item formalises that methodology into a maintained skill in skill/ (installed globally via
scripts/install_pi.sh) and integrates it with the existing agent-log-review skill so "where the time went"
becomes a standard, deterministic section of agent-log-review reports. It should improve on the ad-hoc
analysis where possible (see Design points) rather than merely port it.

## User stories
- As an operator I want to run one command per project and get a deterministic time-attribution report
  (window, session count by kind, active vs blocked vs LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) so I can see
  where agent-hours go without writing throwaway scripts.
- As an operator I want the same skill to flag waste (long blocked waits, hung commands, error-heavy tools,
  retry loops) so I can act on the biggest time sinks.
- As a maintainer of agent-log-review I want the v3 JSONL session parser and signal extractors shared and
  reused so time analysis is consistent with pattern analysis, and reports gain a "Where the time went"
  section.

## Design points (improvements over the throwaway scripts)
- Metrics: per-session AND union (de-duplicated across concurrent sessions) figures for wall, active
  (LLM+tool), LLM durationMs, tool and model split; token economics (input/output/cacheRead, cache-hit %);
  tool-error rates; timezone-correct day windowing; sessions spanning midnight; malformed lines degrade.
- Blocking classification by command intent (wait_for_job waits, test runs, git/build, implement.py
  orchestration, wl, inspection). The 2026-10-21 classifier mis-bucketed a 2.8 h hung node run under "git"
  because the command string contained a git subcommand: primary-binary/first-token attribution plus
  duration-outlier flagging is required, and the report must surface the top-N longest commands.
- Hung-command detection: per-command duration outliers vs typical duration for that command family.
- Report: deterministic Markdown (default) and JSON (--json), --output-file, --cwd/--session-root,
  --max-sessions; optional --parent-id worklog integration mirroring agent-log-review's idempotent comments.
- Integration with agent-log-review: factor the session parser + signal extraction into shared modules
  consumed by both skills; extend agent-log-review's distilled signals with time/blocking/waste features;
  add the time-attribution section to its report and a time-waste category to its classification prompt,
  WITHOUT weakening its privacy guarantees (raw logs never sent to a model; secrets redacted).

## Acceptance criteria
1. A new skill under skill/ with SKILL.md plus scripts/ and tests/ following agent-log-review's structure;
   deterministic CLI with every flag documented in --help.
2. Report covers: window, session count by kind (e.g. audit vs interactive), union active wall time,
   LLM vs tool split, per-tool time/calls/errors, per-model time, token & cache economics, blocking
   classification totals, and top-10 longest bash commands with hang flagging.
3. Union (de-duplicated) and naive-sum figures are both reported and explained: on 2026-10-21 sum-LLM was
   10.0 h vs union 6.5 h; the report must make the double-counting distinction explicit.
4. agent-log-review reports gain the time-attribution section sourced from shared extractors, and its
   classification prompt receives time/waste signals; privacy/redaction guarantees preserved.
5. Automated tests cover: parser/metrics (malformed lines, midnight-spanning sessions, millisecond vs ISO
   timestamps, empty dir, missing usage degrade, no crash) and a golden fixture from the 2026-10-21 AI_Hell
   sessions asserting the headline figures (~8.7 h blocked-wait of ~11.8 h active). Tests run under the
   repo's test policy (test skill).
6. SKILL.md documents usage, metric definitions, limitations (provider durationMs may skew under slot
   contention; host-load correlation initially out of scope) and the integration contract with
   agent-log-review.

## Context and references
- Throwaway working scripts (do not depend on them long-term): /tmp/pi_time/{analyse,deep,final,theme,content}.py
- Session logs: ~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl (v3 format)
- Existing skill to integrate with: skill/agent-log-review (SKILL.md, scripts/agent_log_review.py, tests/) — epic SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC
- Repo conventions: skills live in skill/ with scripts/ and tests/; global install via scripts/install_pi.sh;
  changes affect every project, so they must be tracked here, built, tested, and pushed to dev before re-install;
  UK English; follow existing skill conventions.
- Sample dataset: AI_Hell sessions 2026-10-21 (union active 11.76 h; blocked-wait 8.72 h union / 9.54 h sum
  across 37 waits; hung tune run 2.78 h; test runs ~1.4 h; tokens in 4.3 M / out 0.31 M / cacheRead 118 M;
  plan 7.96 h vs code 2.06 h).
- Use the effort-and-risk skill during planning.

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Do not pipe wait_for_job output through tail/grep to preserve live UI streaming

## Problem statement

When an agent runs `wait_for_job.py` as a bash tool call and pipes its stdout
through `tail -N` / `grep` / `head` (a habit adopted to bound the tool result's
context footprint), the Pi TUI shows **nothing** for the entire wait — the
operator sees only the final "Took 2m 36s" elapsed marker, with no indication
of what the underlying job is doing or whether it is stuck.

## Users

- **Operators / producers** watching an interactive `pi` TUI while the agent
  waits on a background job (e.g. `implement.py finish`, an audit run, a
  release, an epic drive).
  - *User story:* "As an operator watching an agent wait on a 20-minute
    `implement.py finish`, I want the job's progress echoed into the tool box
    as it happens, so I can tell whether the push is running or silently hung."
- **Agents** running the wait — they need a documented, low-context-cost way to
  bound the waiter's verbose output **without** disabling UI streaming.

## Root cause (verified, not speculative)

1. **Pi already streams.** The built-in bash tool emits partial output through
   `onUpdate` → `tool_execution_update` (throttled), and the interactive mode
   updates the pending-tool box on that event
   (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/bash.js`, `modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js`).
2. **The helper already flushes.** `wait_for_job.py` prints every line with
   `flush=True` and emits only *new* job-output lines each poll.
3. **The pipe is the blocker.** `… | tail -25` makes stdout a pipe to `tail`,
   which buffers everything until EOF. Nothing reaches the pi tool's
   `onUpdate` until the wait exits, so the TUI renders an empty box.
4. **The incentive to pipe is real.** Each poll emits both a `progress:` line
   and a `heartbeat:` line (nearly identical), so a 2-hour wait at a 30 s
   interval produces ~500 lines (~10k+ tokens) of near-duplicate text in the
   model's tool result. Agents pipe to avoid that cost — and lose UI feedback
   as a side effect.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deduplicate the per-poll output.** Each poll emits exactly **one** liveness
   line (merge `progress:` + `heartbeat:` into a single line carrying elapsed,
   timeout, and process vitals), so an unpiped wait costs materially less
   model context than today while remaining a visible heartbeat.
2. **Documented anti-pattern.** `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` and
   the `wait_for_job.py` module docstring state explicitly that the waiter's
   output must **not** be piped through `tail`/`head`/`grep` (it buffers and
   kills live UI streaming), and prescribe the supported alternatives for
   bounding context: `--tail-lines`, `--interval`, and relying on pi's own
   result truncation (full log stays at the job's `--log` path).
3. **Skills carry the rule.** The `implement` (and `audit`/`ship`/`test`/`plan`
   where they show a wait invocation) skill docs state the rule next to their
   `wait_for_job.py` example, so agents reading the skill see it at the point
   of use.
4. **Docs-lint test.** A test asserts that no skill doc or shared doc shows a
   recommended `wait_for_job.py` invocation piped through
   `tail`/`head`/`grep` (mirroring `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py`
   conventions), and that the anti-pattern rule is present in the shared doc.
5. **Behavioural test.** Unit test asserts a single liveness line per poll
   (no duplicate `progress:` + `heartbeat:` pair), with existing
   timeout/completion/interrupt and `--json` behaviour unchanged.
6. **Docs updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes (code
   comments/docstrings, shared etiquette doc, skill docs).
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility.** `wait_for_job.py`'s CLI surface and exit codes
  (0/1/2/130) must not change; `--json` output shape must stay
  machine-parseable (`event` keys consumed by callers/tests).
- **No buffering regressions.** Every emitted line must remain `flush=True`;
  the helper must stay usable when stdout *is* a pipe (pi's bash tool always
  pipes stdout — that is fine; only an intermediate buffering command breaks
  streaming).
- **Driven children run `--no-extensions`.** Do not propose a pi extension or
  custom tool as the fix; the repair must live in the helper, its docs, and the
  skill guidance.
- **Silent degradation preserved** when `HERDR_*` env vars are absent.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` (SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK, extended by
  SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA) already emits flushed heartbeats, tails the job's
  output incrementally, and reports process vitals + herdr sidebar state.
- `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` and `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
  already document the feedback channels ("Interactive pi TUI: the bash tool
  streams this partial output live into the tool box").
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` provides the established
  docs-lint pattern for this area.
- **Gap:** nothing forbids or warns about the buffering pipe, and the
  duplicate `progress:`/`heartbeat:` lines actively encourage agents to add one.

## Desired change

A one-line-per-poll waiter whose output streams cleanly into the Pi TUI when
run unpiped; guidance and tests that make "never pipe the waiter" an enforced
convention rather than tribal knowledge.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — deduplicate per-poll liveness output (merge
  `progress:`/`heartbeat:`); docstring anti-pattern note; keep `--json` and
  exit codes unchanged.
- `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` — new "Never pipe the waiter"
  subsection with the supported alternatives.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — rule beside the `wait_for_job.py` examples.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — same rule where
  a wait invocation appears.
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` — docs-lint assertion for the
  buffering anti-pattern (extend existing file).
- `tests/test_wait_for_job_output.py` — new behavioural unit test for the
  single-line-per-poll contract (name indicative; may extend an existing test
  module if one covers this already).

## Related work

- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — *User-visible progress feedback in the Pi agent
  interface during long-running waits (wait_for_job)* (completed) — added the
  live output tailing, process vitals, and completion notification this item
  hardens. This item closes its documented-but-unenforced gap.
- **SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK** — *Background-job wait helper with progress
  heartbeat* (completed) — the helper contract (markers, exit codes) that
  AC1's change must preserve.
- **SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT** — *Roll out background-job etiquette guidance to all
  skills and global docs* (completed) — the rollout whose file list AC3
  extends.
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — *Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts* —
  the wiring table that names `implement.py` as "not appropriate" for the
  helper (unchanged by this item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (verified in pi source):** the interactive TUI updates its
  pending-tool box on `tool_execution_update`, so unpiped output is genuinely
  visible. If a future pi release removes streaming, this item's guidance is
  harmless but its benefit disappears — the docs-lint test still holds value.
- **Assumption:** agents adopt documented rules; enforcement is by docs-lint,
  not runtime. A determined agent could still pipe — acceptable, bounded risk.
- **Scope-creep risk:** it is tempting to also add an extension-provided
  `wait_job` custom tool that streams beautifully. Out of scope (driven
  children run `--no-extensions`); record separately if wanted.
- **Context-cost risk:** fewer lines per poll could mask a genuinely stuck
  job. Mitigation: the single liveness line keeps `state=`/`cpu=`/`children=`
  vitals, which is exactly the signal that distinguishes "alive but quiet"
  from "hung".
- **Compatibility risk:** callers/tests parsing `event:` names (`progress` vs
  `heartbeat`) in text mode could break. Mitigation: AC5 pins the contract and
  existing tests are updated deliberately, not deleted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the missing feedback because pi does not stream bash output, or
  because of how the command was invoked?
  — **Answer (Map, in-session research):** Because of the invocation. Pi's bash
  tool streams partial output via `onUpdate` → `tool_execution_update`
  (`dist/core/tools/bash.js`), and `wait_for_job.py` flushes each line. The
  operator's `… | tail -25` buffers until EOF, so no partial output ever
  reaches the tool box. Evidence: source inspection of the pi bundle plus the
  helper's `print(..., flush=True)` calls.

- **Q:** Was this already delivered by SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA (which explicitly
  covers "live progress in the Pi TUI")?
  — **Answer (Map, in-session research):** Only partially. That item made the
  streaming *possible* and documented it; it did not remove the incentive to
  pipe (duplicate per-poll lines) nor forbid the buffering pipe. Duplicate-work
  check: this item is scoped strictly to the residual gap — no AC duplicates
  the completed item's deliverables.

- **Q:** Should the fix be a pi extension / custom tool that renders progress?
  — **Answer (Map, in-session research):** No. Driven child sessions run
  `--no-extensions` (constraint recorded in SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA), so the fix
  must live in the helper plus skill/docs guidance.

- **Q:** What should an agent do instead of `… | tail -25`?
  — **Answer (Map, in-session research):** Rely on pi's own result truncation
  (it keeps the tail of long output and spills the full text to a temp file),
  and bound volume at the source with `--tail-lines N` and `--interval S`; the
  authoritative job log stays at the path passed to `--log`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)
- **SA-0MLGALPM812GOPDC** – Detect and surface blocking prompts (completed)
- **SA-0MRIIQP9B003T4GK** – Refactor command/refactor.md for conciseness (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 10k, absent, ac1, ac3, ac5 (+327 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvcx570p003vlbk, 10k, absent, ac1, ac3 (+295 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 10k, absent, ac3, acceptance, actively (+263 more)

## Recommended Improvements
1. **Make wait_for_job completion structured and timeout-aware** (feature, target_skill: shared/wait_for_job.py, impact_scope: global)
   Rationale: Long-running jobs were manually polled and one phase timed out after 1800s, while other jobs hit persistence errors. Add PID plus log-pattern completion detection, terminal-state JSON, bounded timeout diagnostics, and no re-polling after terminal failure.
   Sessions: 2026-10-20T19-18-16-613Z_herdr-1792523894-1621863-7345.jsonl, 2026-10-21T12-15-14-857Z_herdr-1792584913-3622638-14477.jsonl, 2026-10-21T17-47-15-515Z_herdr-1792604833-1174629-27228.jsonl
2. **Add canonical worktree and path preflight to implement** (feature, target_skill: implement, impact_scope: global)
   Rationale: Repeated cd/read failures and command retries came from assumed worktree or file paths. Expose WORKTREE_ROOT, verify targets exist before commands, and provide command templates for cross-worktree operations.
   Sessions: 2026-10-21T12-15-12-077Z_herdr-1792584910-3622452-28651.jsonl, 2026-10-21T12-15-14-857Z_herdr-1792584913-3622638-14477.jsonl, 2026-10-21T20-46-45-467Z_herdr-1792615603-2116251-12165.jsonl
3. **Make audit slot and verdict lifecycle idempotent and explicit** (feature, target_skill: audit, impact_scope: global)
   Rationale: Audit phase2 deep jobs timed out, slot acquisition queued, persistence failed, and verdicts were re-asked. Add resumable checkpoints, explicit queued/running/failed states, and idempotent verdict submission so retries do not repeat expensive work.

data.comment:
## Implementation (v5 runtime)

**What changed** (`skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py`):
- Per-keyword `wl search` fan-out now runs concurrently through a bounded
  `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`MAX_SEARCH_WORKERS = 8`). Results are collected in
  keyword order, so aggregation/ranking stays deterministic and
  completion-order independent.
- `collect_results()` runs the repository scan in parallel with the Worklog
  search phase (both consume the same keywords, neither feeds the other).
- `fetch_with_probe()` starts the semantic probe before `wl show`, so the
  probe latency overlaps the fetch instead of following it.
- A keyword whose search raises now yields no results for that keyword
  instead of aborting the batch.
- Constraints honoured: still one `wl search` per keyword (no batching),
  `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` still bounds the fan-out, keyword extraction
  unchanged, analysed item still excluded, report compactness/idempotency
  untouched.

**Measurements** (reference item SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ, 8 searches):
- Fan-out overlap: `search_wall=4.89s sum_of_query_durations=30.51s
  slowest_query=4.87s max_queries_in_flight=8` → batch costs the slowest
  query, not the 30s sum.
- End-to-end against a snapshot copy of the worklog store (removes
  cross-agent `wl`/`wl sync` contention): **3.72s / 4.09s / 4.43s**,
  recall unchanged (3 related items, 3 repo matches).
- Interleaved old-vs-new on the same host at the same moment (identical
  load): pre-v5 20.9s / 28.1s / 47.5s vs v5 10.9s / 11.5s / 22.5s, identical
  recall. Live-store absolute numbers are inflated by other agents'
  worklog traffic — the host was carrying load average 9–44 on 16 cores
  throughout, which is why the <5s figure uses the store snapshot.

**Docs:** `SKILL.md` runtime expectations now state the measured figure
(~2–4s), document `MAX_SEARCH_WORKERS`, the parallel decision-logic steps,
and a `Changes in v5` section.

**Tests:** 11 new tests in `tests/test_find_related.py` (barrier-based
concurrency proof, per-keyword strategy preserved, completion-order
independent ranking/recall, cap bound, failing-search resilience,
self-exclusion, repo-scan/search overlap, probe/fetch overlap, probe
reuse, `_main` wiring).

**Refactor step (implement Step 8):** skipped — the diff is small, the
changed files pass `ruff check`, and the pre-existing smells in this script
are out of scope for this runtime item.

data.comment:
## RCA CORRECTION (2026-10-21) — read before implementing

**This supersedes AC4 and part of the RCA's original F3 as written.** The RCA doc has been corrected (commit 210f3d008, `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md` §5).

**Disproven:** the earlier claim that `not_reviewed` (~L5759) ignores `snapshot_exempt` and therefore contradicts the verdict. Every `not_reviewed` reference (~L5780, ~L5811-5815, ~L5827-5830) is inside the **No** branch, so it cannot drive the verdict. Do not implement that.

**Verified mechanism instead — F3a:** `all_ac_acceptable` (~L5609-5621) folds **child AC verdicts** into the parent's closure with **no** `_child_is_exempt` filter:

```python
child_acs = [a for c in child_results if (...) for a in c.get("ac_results", [])]
all_ac_acceptable = all(r["verdict"] in _ACCEPTABLE_VERDICTS for r in ac_results + child_acs)
```

So a snapshot-exempt child that was re-screened as a side effect into `partial` (infra-fallback/timeout) still forces `Ready to close: No`. This is exactly what happened: all 11 children were `in_review` at audit start, all six parent ACs were `met`/`adjusted`, and the verdict was `No` purely from timeout-tainted `partial` child ACs. The exemption-aware checks that follow (`all_children_reviewed` ~L5633, `any_child_audit_not_ready` ~L5643) are defeated by the aggregation that precedes them.

**F3b (misattribution):** because parent `unmet_count` and `partial_count` are both 0, the report prints "N children not yet in in_review/done stage" (~L5827-5830) — blaming the children's **stages** when the driver was their **AC verdicts**. The report must name the real blocker plus its fallback provenance.

**Why the existing test misses it:** `test_audit_runner_review.py::TestChildExemptionSnapshot::test_snapshot_keeps_parent_yes_when_child_demoted` passes a demoted child with `child_audit_ready=False` but **no `ac_results`**, so the AC-aggregation path is never exercised. Extend the test with tainted child ACs.

**Coordination:** `dev` was red at 2026-10-21T15:22 with 5 audit-skill failures in exactly these paths — `TestChildExemptionSnapshot::test_report_text_honours_snapshot_for_not_reviewed_children` and four `test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` cases (pending gate, 2× unserviced main-slot verdicts, interactive re-run). Reconcile with any in-flight change before rewriting these paths.
